BURHAN:v2p287/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p287/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p287/r5.claim: The blood is falsely alleged to be real evidence; a literal reading is awkward because lying describes speech, not bodies.
BURHAN:v2p287/r5.anchor: اي مكذوب فيه والا لو كان على ظاهره لاشكل لان الكذب من صفات الاقوال لا الأجسام

BURHAN:v2p287/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p287/r6.speaker: الفراء
BURHAN:v2p287/r6.claim: Al-Farra allows كذبا in the accusative as a cognate accusative: جاؤوا implies كذبوا كذبا, as العاديات ضبحا uses a participle with the sense of ضابحات.
BURHAN:v2p287/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء يجوز في النحو بدم كذبا بالنصب على المصدر

ITQAN:v3p103/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p103/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p103/r7.claim: A verbal noun may stand for its object: علم means what is known, صنع what is made, and كذب describes false blood although lying belongs to speech.
ITQAN:v3p103/r7.anchor: وعلى المفعول نحو ﴿ ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه ﴾ أي من معلومه ﴿ صنع الله ﴾ أي مصنوعه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p335/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p335/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p335/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan's variant دم كدب derives from a word for the pale marks on young people's nails, describing blood patterned on the shirt.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p335/r2.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: أصل هذا من الكدب؛ وهو الفوف؛ يعني: البياض الذي يخرج

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r13.claim: “They came over his shirt with blood” places the prepositional phrase as an adverb or circumstantial phrase; scholars dispute placing a non-adverbial circumstantial phrase before it.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r13.anchor: قميصه محله النصب على الظرفية من قوله : بدم أي : جاؤوا فوق قميصه بدم أو على الحالية منه

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r14.claim: Kadhib is an intensive verbal noun describing the blood as false itself, or a passive verbal noun meaning falsely claimed blood.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r14.anchor: ظرفا كذب مصدر وصف به الدم مبالغة ، كأن مجيئهم من الكذب نفسه

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r15.speaker: عائشة
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r15.claim: Aisha’s reading replaces the dotted letter in kadhib with an undotted one, giving a sense of turbid or fresh blood.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r15.anchor: وقرأت عائشة رضي الله عنها بغير المعجمة أي كدب بمعنى كدر أو طري

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r16.claim: The brothers slaughtered a kid and smeared its blood on Joseph’s shirt but forgot to tear the shirt; Jacob wept, then remarked that this was an unusually gentle wolf.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r16.anchor: روى أنهم ذبحوا سخلة ولطخوه بدمها وزل عنهم أن يمزقوه

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r17.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains Jacob’s accusation as meaning their own selves had embellished and made the deed easy for them.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r17.anchor: بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أي : زينت وسهلت قاله ابن عباس

BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r1.claim: “God is the one sought for help” expresses continuous reliance on Him to expose the brothers’ lie and reveal Joseph’s innocence.
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r1.anchor:
والله المستعان أي : المطلوب منه العون وهو إنشاء الاستعانة المستمرة.
على ما تصفون

BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r2.speaker: البيضاوي
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r2.claim: Al-Baydawi says the brothers’ crime preceded their prophethood, if they were prophets; his qualification signals doubt that they were commissioned.
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r2.anchor: قال البيضاوي هذه الجريمة كانت قبل استنبائهم إن صح

BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r3.claim: The author maintains prophets are protected before and after their mission from acts that repel people; the brothers’ envy, assault, throwing Joseph in the well, and deliberate lie are their own acts.
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r3.anchor: وأصاب في ذلك لأن الأنبياء محفوظون قبل نبوتهم كما أنهم معصومون بعدها من الأمور الموجبة للنفرة

BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r8.claim: Inwardly, senses and faculties scheme and deceive, while the faith-lit spirit sees through them and patiently accepts what God’s eternal decree manifests.
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r8.anchor: وفي الآيات إشارات إلى تزوير الحواس والقوى وتلبسها وتمويهاتها وتخيلاتها الفلسفية

BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r9.claim: The Taʾwilat Najmiyya reads Jacob’s appeal for God’s help as asking for patience with the events of divine decree.
BURSEVI:v4p146#2/r9.anchor: وبقوله : {والله المستعان على ما تصفون} يشير إلى الاستعانة بالله على الصبر الجميل

QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r5.claim: Their false bloodied shirt did not persuade Jacob; his heart told him the truth, so he called their story a deception and invoked beautiful patience and God’s help.
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r5.anchor: لم يؤثر تزوير قالبهم في إيجاب تصديق يعقوب - عليه السلام - لكذبهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r6.claim: The hearts of the truthful sense outcomes generally before their details become clear later.
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r6.anchor: وهكذا تقرع قلوب الصديقين عواقب الأمور على وجه الإجمال

QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r7.claim: They were punished for failing to tear Joseph’s shirt, allowing Jacob to recognize their lie.
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r7.anchor: عوقبوا على ما فعلوه بأن أغفلوا عن تمزيق قميصه

TUSTARI:12:18/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:12:18/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:12:18/r1.claim: Beautiful patience is patience with contentment, marked by the absence of despair; knowing God is with you and recalling the ease of well-being make it possible.
TUSTARI:12:18/r1.anchor: قال: الصبر مع الرضا. قيل: ما علامته؟ قال: أن لا يجزع فيه.

TUSTARI:12:18/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:12:18/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:12:18/r2.claim: Patience is like a cup with patience on top and honey beneath; he wonders how anyone could fail to endure when God says He is with the patient.
TUSTARI:12:18/r2.anchor: فإنما مثل الصبر مثل قدح أعلاه الصبر وأسفله العسل. ثم قال: عجبت ممن لم يصبروا

FARRA:v2p39/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p39/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p39/r1.claim: فصبر جميل is nominative as a noun phrase; فصبرا جميلا is also possible as a direct command to oneself, and Ubayy reads the accusative form.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#3/r1.claim: بدم كذب means with blood falsely attributed to Joseph, or fabricated blood.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#3/r1.anchor: على قميصه بدم كذب} أي: مكذوب به

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p213#3/r2.claim: سولت means adorned or made attractive, as in Satan's making their deeds seem attractive.

MAJAZ:v1p303/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p303/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p303/r1.claim: فصبر جميل is nominative because جميل modifies الصبر; without the adjective, Arabs would use the accusative command صبرا.

MAJAZ:v1p303/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p303/r2.speaker: الراجز
MAJAZ:v1p303/r2.claim: A rajaz poem uses صبر جميل as a nominative noun phrase with an adjective.
MAJAZ:v1p303/r2.anchor: قال [الراجز] : يشكو إلى جملى طول السرى

MAJAZ:v1p303/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p303/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن الأثرم
MAJAZ:v1p303/r3.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Athram heard someone recite صبرا جميل as a vocative, meaning “O Jamīl.”
MAJAZ:v1p303/r3.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الأثرم: سمعت من ينشد: صبرا جميل

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r1.claim: Jacob reasoned that a beast would have torn Joseph's shirt if it had eaten him.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله وجاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب قال : لو كان اكله السبع

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r2.claim: The false blood came from a lamb or young sheep.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس في قوله : بدم كذب قال : كان دم سخلة - وروى ، عن مجاهد انه قال : سخلة شاة .

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r3.speaker: الشعبي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r3.claim: The shirt was one of three signs: its lack of tears disproved the brothers' claim that a wolf ate Joseph.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r3.anchor: عن سماك ، عن الشعبي قال : كانت في قميص يوسف ثلاث آيات حيث جاءوا بقميصه إلى أبيه ، فقالوا : اكله الذئب فقال ابوه : لو اكله الذئب لشق قميصه .

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r4.claim: The brothers stained the shirt with deer blood; Jacob saw no tooth or claw marks and called the wolf merciful.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r4.anchor: عن قتادة : قوله : وجاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب قال : صادوا ظبيا فذبحوه فلطخوا به القميص ، فجعل يقلب القميص فيقول : ما ارى به اثر ناب ولا ظفر

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r5.claim: Jacob wept with the bloody shirt over his face and said the wolf was merciful for not tearing it.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r5.anchor: عن السدى قال : فبكى الشيخ وصاح باعلى صوته ، ثم قال : اين القميص ؟ فجاءوا بقميصه عليه دم كذب

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r6.claim: The brothers' own selves prompted them to do what they did.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r6.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس ، قوله : قال بل سولت لكم انفسكم امرا قال : امرتكم انفسكم .

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r7.claim: Their selves made the deed seem attractive to them.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r7.anchor: قتادة قوله قال بل سولت لكم انفسكم امرا

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r8.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r8.claim: Beautiful patience means making no complaint.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2111/r8.anchor: عن حبان بن ابى جبلة قال : سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، عن قوله : فصبر جميل قال : لا شكوى فيه .

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r1.claim: Beautiful patience contains no despair or distress.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : فصبر جميل قال : ليس فيه جزع .

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r2.claim: Beautiful patience has no lament except complaint directed to God.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r2.anchor: عن الحسن ، قال : الصبر الجميل : الذي ليس فوقه جزع الا إلى الله .

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r3.claim: What the brothers ascribe means what they falsely claim.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r3.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : والله المستعان على ما تصفون اي : تكذبون .

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r4.claim: Jacob recognized his sons' plot and sought God's help; God allowed Jacob's grief and Joseph's enslavement as a test, though He could have stopped the brothers.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2112/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق ، قوله : والله المستعان على ما تصفون فعرف ، يعني : يعقوب ان قد كادوه واستعان الله على ما يسمع من قولهم لما بلغ كرب ذلك منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r1.claim: The phrase on his shirt is a circumstantial phrase belonging to blood, placed before its head noun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { على قميصه } حال من ( دم ) فقدم على صاحب الحال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r2.claim: Bal rejects the brothers' claim that a wolf ate Joseph and explicitly calls their story false; taswila means making attractive what the self wants to obtain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r2.anchor: حرف الإضراب إبطال لدعواهم أن الذئب أكله فقد صرح لهم بكذبهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r3.claim: The vague matter could have been killing, selling, or banishing Joseph; its indefinite form makes their act sound ominous.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r3.anchor: والإبهام الذي في كلمة { أمرا } يحتمل عدة أشياء مما يمكن أن يؤذوا به يوسف عليه السلام : من قتل ، أو بيع ، أو تغريب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r4.claim: Beautiful patience stands for a command to be patient; its nominative form conveys firmness and duration, and may be an aside to the sons, a self-address, or an elliptical statement of Jacob's affair, with the exhortative reading strongest.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r4.anchor: عدل به عن النصب إلى الرفع للدلالة على الثبات والدوام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r5.claim: Ibrahim ibn Kunyaf al-Nahshali's poem says patience is more beautiful for a free person than there being no reliance against time, illustrating a possible descriptive use of beautiful.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r5.anchor:
كما قال إبراهيم بن كنيف النبهاني :
تصبر فإن الصبر بالحر أجمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r6.claim: Beautiful may specify patience free from agitation, rather than merely explain that patience is good; its beauty is the most excellent, unblemished state of patience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون وصفا مخصصا . وقد فسر الصبر الجميل بالذي لا يخالطه جزع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r7.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r7.claim: In an author-described sound hadith, the Prophet told a grieving woman to fear God and be patient; after learning who he was, she returned, and he said complete patience is at the first shock.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p238#2/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح أن النبي عليه السلام مر بامرأة تبكي عند قبر فقال لها : ( اتقي الله واصبري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p241/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p241/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p241/r1.claim: Jacob's statement about God as the one sought for help may be a prayer for aid or a report that he relies on God to endure, and may also ask God to free Joseph.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p241/r1.anchor: فتكون محتملة للمعنيين المذكورين من إنشاء الاستعانة أو الإخبار بحصول استعانته بالله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p241/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p241/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p241/r2.claim: What you describe is deliberately open-ended: Jacob knows his sons are lying and harmed Joseph but not exactly how; they mean the wolf's supposed killing, while Jacob means the actual injury, resembling 37:180.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p241/r2.anchor: لأنه كان واثقا بأنهم كاذبون في الصفة وواثقا بأنهم ألحقوا بيوسف عليه السلام ضرا فلما لم يتعين عنده المصاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p241/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p241/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p241/r3.claim: Jacob leaves the matter to God because old age and lack of allies make him unable to uncover Joseph's fate without his sons; once he has an opportunity, he tells them to search for Joseph and his brother.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p241/r3.anchor: ولأنه لا عضد له يستعين به على أبنائه أولئك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r1.claim: Prophets may mistake a liar for a truthful person before revelation; they remain human and judge by what they hear.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r2.claim: The Prophet believed ʿAbd Allah b. Ubayy and disbelieved Zayd b. Arqam about the latter's report until revelation disclosed the truth.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r3.claim: Joseph's brothers used sophistry and argument; their case did not compel Yaʿqub to obstinate denial.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r3.anchor: فكلام اخوة يوسف إنما هو مغالطة ومحاجة لا إلزام عناد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r4.claim: They killed a young sheep or kid, stained Joseph's shirt, and showed it to Jacob; he found no tear or tooth mark and inferred their lie.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r5.claim: Jacob challenged them that a wolf could not eat Joseph while leaving his shirt un-torn; this was his circumstantial proof.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r6.claim: Malik's legal school used this episode to support acting on circumstantial signs in matters such as the oath of group liability (qasama).

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r7.speaker: الشافعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r7.claim: The shirt held three signs: it exposed their lie, testified by its tear, and later restored Jacob's sight.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r7.anchor: قال الشافعي: كان في القميص ثلاث آيات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r8.claim: Another report says the brothers smeared a wolf's mouth with blood; Jacob summoned it, and it crouched and spoke to deny their story.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r8.anchor: وروي أنهم ذهبوا فأخذوا ذئبا فلطخوا فاه بالدم وساقوه وقالوا ليعقوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r9.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r9.claim: Al-Tabari takes kadhib as either blood associated with a lie or blood falsely accused; he cites a poetic analogy with maʿqūl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r9.anchor: هذا كلام الطبري، ولا شاهد له فيه عندي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r10.claim: The author rejects al-Tabari's evidence and reads kadhib as a verbal noun used adjectivally for emphasis.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r11.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r11.claim: Al-Hasan reads the word with an unpointed dāl, giving the sense of fresh blood or similar; the author considers this reading weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227/r11.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: «بدم كذب» بدال غير معجمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r1.claim: Sawwalat means that the souls made the matter pleasing and desired: they had contrived an ugly deed against Joseph.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r2.claim: The nominative fa-sabrun jamīl can be parsed with an omitted subject, meaning my affair is beautiful patience, or an omitted predicate, meaning beautiful patience is better.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r2.anchor: فصبر جميل رفع إما على حذف الابتداء وإما على حذف الخبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r3.speaker: الأشهب وعيسى بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r3.claim: They read fa-ṣabran jamīlan in the accusative with an implied verb; the same reading is reported in the codices of Ubayy and Anas.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r4.claim: Sibawayh regards the accusative reading as weak, since this construction is suitable only with an imperative; the author says it works if Jacob turns to address himself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r4.anchor: وهي قراءة ضعيفة عند سيبويه ولا يصلح النصب في مثل هذا إلا مع الأمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r5.claim: Poetic lines illustrate the imperative accusative and a nominative reading construed as addressing a camel; the accusative here can be saved by Jacob speaking to himself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r5.anchor: وإنما تصح قراءة النصب على أن تقدر يعقوب عليه السلام رجع إلى مخاطبة نفسه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r6.claim: Beautiful patience means not voicing one's complaint to another human; a Prophetic report says the one who broadcasts hardship has not shown beautiful patience.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p227#2/r7.claim: Saying God is the source of help expresses submission to God's decree and reliance on Him to bear what the brothers describe.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r1.claim: “False blood” means blood in which a lie was made: Arabic often uses a verbal noun in the passive-object sense, as in maʿqūl for reason and majlūd for skin; al-Farra, al-Akhfash, al-Zajjaj, and Ibn Qutayba explain the usage, with poetry as evidence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r1.anchor: معناه بدم مكذوب فيه والعرب تجعل المصدر في كثير من الكلام مفعولا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says they killed a young goat and dipped Joseph’s shirt in its blood; Jacob noticed the shirt was untorn and said a wolf would have torn it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس أخذوا جديا فذبحوه ثم غمسوا قميص يوسف في دمه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r3.claim: Qatada says the blood on the shirt was from a gazelle.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r4.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads kadhaban in the accusative; Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, and Abu al-ʿAliya read kadhb with an unpointed dhal, meaning fresh blood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p192/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة بدم كذبا بالنصب وقرأ ابن عباس والحسن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r1.claim: The brothers used fabricated blood to reinforce their plot, slaughtering a young lamb and smearing Joseph's shirt but forgetting to tear it; Jacob sees through their scheme and commits to beautiful patience and God's help against their lies.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r1.anchor: فذبحوها، ولطخوا ثوب يوسف بدمها، موهمين أن هذا قميصه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Shaʿbī, al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, and others infer that a wolf would have torn the shirt if it had eaten Joseph.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r2.anchor: قال: لو أكله السبع لخرق القميص

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r3.claim: Beautiful patience is patience without distress or agitation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: الصبر الجميل: الذي لا جزع فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r4.speaker: حبان بن أبي جبلة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r4.claim: A disconnected report attributes to the Prophet the definition of beautiful patience as patience without complaint.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r5.speaker: الثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r5.claim: A saying attributed by al-Thawrī to one of his companions lists three forms of patience: do not mention your pain, misfortune, or praise yourself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r5.anchor: ثلاث من الصبر: ألا تحدث بوجعك، ولا بمصيبتك، ولا تزكي نفسك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r6.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r6.claim: During the slander incident, ʿĀʾishah compared herself and her accusers to Joseph's father, invoking beautiful patience and God's help against what they described.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p375#2/r6.anchor: والله لا أجد لي ولكم مثلا إلا أبا يوسف

JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r1.speaker: عائشة
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r1.claim: The common reading is ḏal with zāy in ‘lying blood’; ʿĀʾisha's reading uses dāl and means fresh blood.
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة: بدم كذب بالذال معجمة من فوق، وعن عائشة: بدم [كدب] بالدال

JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r2.speaker: قطرب
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r2.claim: The nominative fa-ṣabrun jamīl presumes ‘my patience’ or ‘my way’ as subject; Qutrub reports the implied-noun parsing.
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r2.anchor: وقراءة العامة: فصبر جميل على تقدير: صبري صبر جميل

JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r3.speaker: أشهب العقيلي
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r3.claim: He reads fa-ṣabran jamīlan as an accusative cognate expression meaning ‘I shall patiently endure’; other explanations exhort the self or prefer patience over grief.
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ أشهب العقيلي: فصبرا جميلا على المصدر

JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r4.speaker: ذو الرمة
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r4.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's line exemplifies the accusative form ṣabran jamīlan used as a verbal noun.
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r4.anchor: قال ذو الرمة: ألا إنما مي فصبرا بلية

JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r5.claim: A line beginning ‘my camel complains’ witnesses ṣabrun jamīl as a nominative sentence, meaning beautiful patience is preferable to complaint.
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r5.anchor: فأما الرفع فقال الشاعر: يشكوا إلي جملي طول السرى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r1.claim: Dam kadhib means false blood, either a noun describing it or source-word hyperbole as though blood itself were falsehood.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r1.anchor: {بدم كذب } ذي كذب . أو وصف بالمصدر مبالغة ، كأنه نفس الكذب وعينه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r2.claim: A reading has kadhiban in the accusative as a circumstantial expression or causal object.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r2.anchor: وقرىء : ( كذبا ) نصبا على الحال ، بمعنى جاءوا به كاذبين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r3.speaker: عائشة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r3.claim: ʿĀʾisha reads kadb with dāl, meaning cloudy or, alternatively, fresh; Ibn Jinnī derives it from white spots on young people’s nails.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r3.anchor: وقرأت عائشة رضي الله عنها : كدب ، بالدال غير المعجمة ، أي كدر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r4.claim: One report says the brothers slaughtered a lamb and smeared its blood on the shirt, forgetting to tear it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r4.anchor: روي أنهم ذبحوا سخلة ولطخوه بدمها ، وزل عنهم أن يمزقوه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r5.claim: Jacob asked for the shirt, put it on his face, and cried until blood stained him; he remarked that no wolf was more patient, eating a son without tearing the shirt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r5.anchor: وروي أن يعقوب لما سمع بخبر يوسف صاح بأعلى صوته وقال : أين القميص ؟

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r6.claim: The shirt had three signs: it exposed the brothers’ lie, restored Jacob’s sight on his face, and proved Joseph innocent when torn from behind.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r6.anchor: وقيل كان في قميص يوسف ثلاث آيات : كان دليلا ليعقوب على كذبهم ، وألقاه على وجهه فارتد بصيرا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r7.claim: ʿAlā qamīṣihi is an adverbial accusative meaning ‘above his shirt’; a genitive’s circumstantial phrase cannot precede it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r7.anchor: محله النصب على الظرف ، كأنه قيل : وجاءوا فوق قميصه بدم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r8.claim: Sawwalat means made easy, from a root suggesting slackness; Jacob inferred the deed from known envy and the intact shirt, or learned by revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r8.anchor: { سولت } سهلت من السول وهو الاسترخاء ، أي : سهلت { لكم أنفسكم أمرا } عظيما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r9.claim: Fa-ṣabrun jamīl may be a predicate or topic; Ubayy reads fa-ṣabran jamīlan.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r9.anchor: { فصبر جميل } خبر أو مبتدأ لكونه موصوفا أي فأمري صبر جميل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r10.claim: A Prophetic report defines beautiful patience as patience without complaint to people, consistent with Jacob’s words in 12:86.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r10.anchor: والصبر الجميل جاء في الحديث المرفوع . ( 540 ) ( أنه الذي لا شكوى فيه إلى الخلق )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r11.speaker: وقيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r11.claim: Another interpretation is that Jacob would not meet them with a gloomy face but treat them as before.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r11.anchor: وقيل : لا أعايشكم على كآبة الوجه ، بل أكون لكم كما كنت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r12.claim: A report says Jacob’s brows fell over his eyes from grief; when God asked if he complained of Him, Jacob called it his fault and asked forgiveness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r12.anchor: فأوحى الله تعالى إليه : يا يعقوب أتشكوني ؟ قال : يا رب . خطيئة فاغفرها لي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r13.claim: ‘God is the one whose help is sought’ means Jacob asks God to help endure Joseph’s loss and the brothers’ account.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p425/r13.anchor: أي أستعينه { على } احتمال { ما تصفون } من هلاك يوسف والصبر على الرزء فيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r10.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r10.claim: The false blood on Joseph's shirt was the blood of a lamb.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r11.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r11.claim: The false blood was the blood of a deer.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r12.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r12.claim: Jacob saw that the shirt was not torn and remarked that the wolf was unusually gentle to eat his son while sparing his shirt.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r12.anchor: يا بني والله ما عهدت الذئب حليما أيأكل ابني ويبقي على قميصه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r13.claim: Blood described as kadhib is fabricated blood; the verbal noun is used adjectivally, meaning blood marked by falsehood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r13.anchor: أي مكذوب فيه , ولكن وصفه بالمصدر فصار تقديره بدم ذي كذب

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r14.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r14.claim: Al-Hasan read the word with an undotted د, meaning changed or discolored blood, according to al-Shaʿbī.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r14.anchor: وقرأ الحسن { بدم كذب } بالدال غير معجمة , ومعناه بدم متغير قاله الشعبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r15.claim: Joseph's shirt marks three signs: false blood, a tear from behind, and its being placed on Jacob's face so his sight returned.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r15.anchor: وفي القميص ثلاث آيات : حين جاءوا عليه بدم كذب , وحين قد قميصه من دبر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r16.claim: Sawwalat lakum anfusukum means your souls commanded the deed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r16.anchor: بل أمرتكم أنفسكم , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r17.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r17.claim: Sawwalat lakum anfusukum means your souls adorned the deed for you.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r17.anchor: بل زينت لكم أنفسكم أمرا , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r18.claim: Jacob's rejection of their story may have come by revelation, prior knowledge from God, or a correct inference and intuition.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r18.anchor: أنه كان ذلك بوحي من الله تعالى إليه بعد فعلهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r19.claim: “Beautiful patience” may mean forgiving the brothers' conduct, or bearing the grief of losing Joseph.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r19.anchor: الصبر على مقابلتهم على فعلهم فيكون هذا الصبر عفوا عن مؤاخذتهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r20.claim: The phrase may state that patience is beautiful, or command Jacob to practice beautiful patience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r20.anchor: أنه بمعنى أن من الجميل أن أصبر . الثاني : أنه أمر نفسه بصبر جميل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r21.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r21.claim: Beautiful patience is patience without lamentation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r21.anchor: أنه الصبر الذي لا جزع فيه قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r22.claim: Beautiful patience may mean patience without complaint; a report from the Prophet says that whoever voices complaint has not been patient.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r22.anchor: روى حباب بن أبي حبلة قال : سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قوله تعالى { فصبر جميل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r23.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r23.claim: Seeking God's help may mean seeking help to bear the beautiful patience, bear the brothers' account, or endure their lies.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r23.anchor: يعني على ما تكذبون , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r24.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r24.claim: God tested Jacob in old age and Joseph in youth to see their resolve.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p14/r24.anchor: ابتلى الله يعقوب في كبره , ويوسف في صغره لينظر كيف عزمهما

MUJAHID:v1p311#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p311#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p311#2/r1.claim: The blood placed on Joseph's shirt was the blood of a young goat or sheep.
MUJAHID:v1p311#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وجاؤوا على قميصه بدم كذب ﴾ يعني بدم سخلة شاة

MUJAHID:v1p311#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p311#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p311#2/r2.claim: Beautiful patience is patience without complaint or agitation.
MUJAHID:v1p311#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ فصبر جميل ﴾ يقول صبر ليس فيه جزع

MUQATIL:12:16-18/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:16-18/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:16-18/r2.claim: After throwing Joseph into the well, the brothers stripped his shirt and put a slaughtered lamb’s blood on it; seeing it intact, Jacob suspects them and wryly says the wolf spared the garment.
MUQATIL:12:16-18/r2.anchor: وذلك أنهم حين ألقوه في البئر انتزعوا ثيابه، وهو قميصه،

MUQATIL:12:16-18/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:16-18/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:16-18/r3.claim: Jacob says his patience will be beautiful, without despair, and seeks God’s help against their account; he cried and could not sleep or eat, which Muqatil says explains Jewish wailing when reading Torah.
MUQATIL:12:16-18/r3.anchor: يعنى صبرى صبرا حسنا لا جزع فيه،

NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r1.claim: Blood described as كذب either means blood connected with a lie or uses a verbal noun as an intensified adjective, as when a liar is called falsehood itself.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r1.anchor: ذى كذب أو وصف بالمصدر مبالغة كأنه نفس الكذب ويعنه كما يقال للكذاب هو الكذب بعينه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r2.claim: One report says they slaughtered a lamb, stained Joseph's shirt with its blood, and forgot to tear it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r2.anchor: روى أنهم ذبحوا سخلة ولطخواالقميص بدمها وزل عنهم أن يمزقوه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r3.claim: Another report has Jacob demand the shirt, cast it over his face, and cry until the shirt's blood stained his face; he remarks that no wolf was ever so gentle as to eat his son without tearing the shirt.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r3.anchor: وأخذه وألقاه على وجهه وبكى حتى خضب وجهه بدم القميص وقال تالله

NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r4.claim: The shirt had three signs: it proved the brothers lied, restored Jacob's sight when placed on his face, and showed Joseph's innocence because it was torn from behind.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r4.anchor: وقيل كان فى قميص يوسف ثلاث آيات كان دليلا ليعقوب على كذبهم وألقاه على وجهه فارتد بصيرا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r5.claim: The phrase على قميصه is an adverbial expression meaning the blood was over the shirt.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r5.anchor: ومحل على قميصه النصب على الظرف كأنه قيل وجاءوا فوق قميصه بدم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r6.claim: Jacob says their selves made an immense deed seem attractive or easy to them.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r6.anchor: ﴿ بل سولت ﴾ زينت أوسهلت ﴿ لكم أنفسكم أمرا ﴾ عظيما ارتكبتموه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r7.claim: Ṣabr jamīl can be parsed as a predicate or a subject with an omitted predicate; the most beautiful patience is making no complaint to people.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r7.anchor: ﴿ فصبر جميل ﴾ خبر أو مبتدأ لكونه موصوفا أى فأمرى صبر جميل

NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r8.claim: Jacob seeks God's help in bearing what they claim about Joseph's death and the grief of his loss.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#4/r8.anchor: ﴿ والله المستعان ﴾ أى أستعينه ﴿ على ﴾ احتمال ﴿ ما تصفون ﴾ من هلاك يوسف والصبر على الرزء فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r1.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r1.claim: Mujahid says the forged blood was from a slaughtered sheep or young goat; Qatada says it was from a gazelle.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: كان دم سخلة أو جدي

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r2.claim: “Kazib” describes the blood as a verbal noun meaning falsified or lied-about blood, like calling the inhabitants “the village” or using a verbal noun for the agent or object.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r2.anchor: أي جاءوا على قميصه بدم مكذوب فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r3.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r3.claim: Hasan and ʿAʾisha read “kadib” with dāl, meaning fresh blood; al-Shaʿbi also says it can mean changed blood, and the word may refer to the white mark on a youth's fingernail, like the contrasting colors on the shirt.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r4.claim: God paired the brothers' blood-stained-shirt sign with a contrary sign: a wolf could not have eaten Joseph while leaving the shirt un-torn; Jacob noticed no hole or trace and inferred their lie.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r4.anchor: قرن الله بهذه العلامة علامة تعارضها

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Jacob said the wolf would have torn the shirt if it had eaten Joseph; one transmission says the blood came from a young goat.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان الدم دم سخلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r6.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r6.claim: Al-Mawardi says the shirt bears three signs, but Qurtubi rejects this because the bloodied, torn, and later healing shirts are different garments; one alternative identifies the torn shirt with the one brought by the herald.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r6.anchor: وحكى الماوردي أن في القميص ثلاث آيات:

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r7.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r7.claim: A report from al-Hasan says the brothers also claimed robbers had killed Joseph; their changing explanation increased Jacob's suspicion, since robbers would have taken the shirt and a wolf would have torn it.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r7.anchor: وروي أنهم قالوا له: بل اللصوص قتلوه

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r8.claim: Jurists use the episode to support circumstantial evidence in cases such as sworn group liability: Jacob inferred the lie from the intact shirt, and judges should assess competing signs and rule according to the stronger indication; Ibn al-ʿArabi says there is no disagreement in acting on such evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18/r8.anchor: استدل الفقهاء بهذه الآية في إعمال الأمارات

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r1.claim: An extended, unsourced narrative says Jacob asked for some trace of Joseph; the brothers showed his bloodied but un-torn shirt, leading Jacob to accuse them. They plotted to kill him, but Judah stopped them; they then brought a wolf tied and bloodied, which God enabled to speak and deny eating Joseph, saying he was a stranger searching for his own missing brother. Jacob released it and declared the brothers had proved their own guilt.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r1.anchor: روي أن يعقوب لما قالوا له: «فأكله الذئب» قال لهم:

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r2.claim: “Sawwalt” means embellished or made attractive: their souls had decorated some affair other than the one they described.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj understands “fa-sabrun jamil” as saying that Jacob's own state and belief would be beautiful patience.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: أي فشأني والذي أعتقده

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r4.speaker: قطرب
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r4.claim: Qutrub takes the phrase to mean “my patience is beautiful patience.”
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r4.anchor: وقال قطرب: أي فصبري صبر جميل

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation says beautiful patience is what is better for Jacob, with an omitted predicate after the subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: أي فصبر جميل أولى بي

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet defined beautiful patience as patience without complaint; Qurtubi says fuller discussion will appear at the end of the sura.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r1.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عن الصبر الجميل فقال:

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r2.claim: Abu Hatim says ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar read “fa-sabran jamilan” in the accusative, as did al-Ashhab al-ʿUqayli and the codices of Anas and Abu Salih.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r2.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: قرأ عيسى بن عمر

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r3.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad prefers the nominative “fa-sabrun jamil” because it means “My Lord, I have beautiful patience”; the accusative is an absolute object meaning “I will surely be patient.” A poem illustrates the latter construction.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r3.anchor: المبرد: «فصبر جميل» بالرفع أولى من النصب

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r4.claim: Beautiful patience has no distress or complaint; another interpretation says Jacob did not treat his sons with a gloomy face but continued to interact normally, indicating that he forgave them.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r4.anchor: والصبر الجميل هو الذي لا جزع فيه ولا شكوى

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r5.speaker: حبيب بن أبي ثابت
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r5.claim: Habib ibn Abi Thabit recounts that Jacob's eyebrows fell over his eyes from long years and grief; when God asked if he was complaining of Him, Jacob confessed a sin and asked forgiveness.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r5.anchor: وعن حبيب بن أبي ثابت أن يعقوب كان قد سقط حاجباه على عينيه

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r6.claim: “God is the one whose help is sought” is a nominal sentence, subject and predicate; Jacob seeks help in bearing what his sons falsely describe.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r7.speaker: ابن أبي رفاعة
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abi Rifaʿa advises prudent people to question their own judgment: Jacob correctly suspected his sons' account of Joseph's disappearance, but later failed to do so when they said Benjamin had stolen and repeated that their souls had embellished an affair.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:18#3/r7.anchor: قال ابن أبي رفاعة: ينبغي لأهل الرأي

RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that the brothers' selves embellished an act for them.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : معناه : بل زينت لكم أنفسكم أمرا .

RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r2.speaker: الأزهري
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r2.claim: Al-Azharī relates taswīl to a person's wish or request, which beautifies what the seeker wants, including falsehood; the original hamza was avoided as burdensome.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r2.anchor: قال الأزهري : كأن التسويل تفعيل من سؤال الإنسان ، وهو أمنيته التي يطلبها فتزين لطالبها الباطل وغيره

RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī derives sawwalat from sawl, meaning ease or relaxation.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r3.anchor: وقال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { سولت } سهلت من السول وهو الاسترخاء .

RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r4.claim: Bal rejects the wolf account: the brothers' selves adorned a different deed from what they described.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r4.anchor: إذا عرفت هذا فنقول : قوله : { بل } رد لقولهم : { أكله الذئب } كأنه قال : ليس كما تقولون : { بل سولت لكم أنفسكم }

RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r5.claim: Jacob may have recognized their lie from his knowledge of their intense envy, or because God's promise to choose Joseph meant Joseph was alive.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r5.anchor: أنه كان يعرف الحسد الشديد في قلوبهم

RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the bloodied shirt was not torn, so Jacob knew a wolf had not eaten Joseph.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r6.anchor: القول الثالث : قال سعيد بن جبير : لما جاؤا على قميصه بدم كذب ، وما كان متخرقا ، قال كذبتم لو أكله الذئب لخرق قميصه

RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r7.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddī says Jacob remarked that this wolf was merciful, eating Joseph's flesh without tearing his shirt.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r7.anchor: وعن السدي أنه قال : إن يعقوب عليه السلام قال : إن هذا الذئب كان رحيما ، فكيف أكل لحمه ولم يخرق قميصه ؟

RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r8.claim: The brothers then suggested robbers killed Joseph; Jacob challenged that account because robbers would have wanted the shirt more than the killing, and their conflicting stories exposed them.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r8.anchor: فلما اختلفت أقوالهم عرف بسبب ذلك كذبهم

RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r9.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r9.claim: The phrase fa-ṣabrun jamīl is parsed as a fronted predicate with the subject omitted: “what I do is beautiful patience.”
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r9.anchor: قال الخليل : الذي أفعله صبر جميل .

RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r10.speaker: قطرب
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r10.claim: Quṭrub parses the phrase to mean “my patience is beautiful patience.”
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r10.anchor: وقال قطرب : معناه : فصبري صبر جميل .

RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r11.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ supplies an omitted pronoun: “so it is beautiful patience.”

RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r12.speaker: عائشة
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r12.claim: In the account of the slander, ʿĀʾisha compares her predicament with Jacob and his sons, invoking his beautiful patience; God then revealed her vindication.
RAZI-FULL:v18p82#2/r12.anchor: وروي عن عائشة رضي الله عنها في قصة الإفك أنها قالت : والله لئن حلفت لا تصدقوني وإن اعتذرت لا تعذروني

RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r1.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that the Prophet explained beautiful patience as patience without complaint: whoever tells others of the affliction has not endured patiently.
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r1.anchor: عن الحسن أنه سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قوله : { فصبر جميل } فقال : ( صبر لا شكوى فيه فمن بث لم يصبر )

RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r2.claim: Qur'an 12:86 illustrates that true complaint is directed to God.
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r2.anchor: ويدل عليه من القرآن قوله تعالى : { إنما أشكو بثى وحزنى إلى الله }

RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r3.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r3.claim: Mujāhid explains beautiful patience as patience without agitation or despair.
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد : فصبر جميل ، أي من غير جزع

RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r4.speaker: الثوري
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r4.claim: Al-Thawrī says patience means not talking about one's pain or misfortune and not praising oneself.
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r4.anchor: وقال الثوري : من الصبر أن لا تحدث بوجعك ولا بمصيبتك ، ولا تزكي نفسك

RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r5.claim: The author challenges Jacob's passivity: patience with God's decree is required, but injustice by wrongdoers must be removed, especially when it harms another; Jacob should have searched for Joseph or sought justice.
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r5.anchor: وههنا بحث وهو أن الصبر على قضاء الله تعالى واجب فأما الصبر على ظلم الظالمين ، ومكر الماكرين فغير واجب ، بل الواجب إزالته

RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r6.claim: The problem sharpens if Jacob knew from God's promise that Joseph was safe: Jacob had status and support, so a thorough search could have exposed the deception and rescued Joseph.
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r6.anchor: وأيضا إن يعقوب عليه السلام كان رجلا عظيم القدر في نفسه ، وكان من بيت عظيم شريف

RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r7.claim: The author says no answer exists except that God barred Jacob from searching to intensify his trial; perhaps the brothers could have harmed him, he trusted God's protection and Joseph's future, or he avoided exposing and punishing his sons, so surrender seemed best.
RAZI-FULL:v18p83/r7.anchor: لا جواب عنه إلا أن يقال إنه سبحانه وتعالى منعه عن الطلب تشديدا للمحنة عليه

RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r1.claim: Beautiful patience recognizes God as the source of the trial and owner of all things, so the heart is absorbed in this and does not complain.
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r1.anchor: الصبر الجميل هو أن يعرف أن منزل ذلك البلاء هو الله تعالى ، ثم يعلم أن الله سبحانه مالك الملك

RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r2.claim: It also trusts that the one who sends the trial is wise, knowing, watchful, remembering, and merciful, so everything He does is wise and right.
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r2.anchor: الوجه الثاني : أنه يعلم أن منزل هذا البلاء ، حكيم لا يجهل ، وعالم لا يغفل ، عليم لا ينسى رحيم لا يطغى

RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r3.claim: A third form arises from beholding God in the trial: perfect love does not grow with favor or shrink with harshness; love based on reward would only love the benefit instrumentally.
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r3.anchor: المحبة التامة لا تزداد بالوفاء ولا تنقص بالجفاء

RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r4.claim: Patience motivated by anything other than acceptance of God's decree is not beautiful; the general test for good acts, words, and beliefs is whether they seek servitude to God.
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r4.anchor: كل ما كان لطلب عبودية الله تعالى كان حسنا وإلا فلا

RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r5.claim: An attributed saying urges a person to consult the heart even if jurists give opinions, and examine whether worship truly motivates him; knowledge that is not true inwardly gives no benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r5.anchor: وههنا يظهر صدق ما روي في الأثر ( استفت قلبك / ولو أفتاك المفتون )

RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r6.claim: Jacob can only be patient through God's help because strong natural impulses toward grief contend with spiritual impulses toward patience and acceptance.
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r6.anchor: أن إقدامه على الصبر لا يمكن إلا بمعونة الله تعالى ، لأن الدواعي النفسانية تدعوه إلى إظهار الجزع

RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r7.claim: “Beautiful patience” parallels “You alone we worship,” while asking God for help parallels “You alone we ask for help,” both from al-Fātiḥa 1:5.
RAZI-FULL:v18p84/r7.anchor: فقوله : { فصبر جميل } يجري مجرى قوله : { إياك نعبد } ( الفاتحة : 5 ) وقوله : { والله المستعان على ما تصفون } يجري مجرى قوله : { وإياك نستعين } ( الفاتحة : 5 )

SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r1.claim: على قميصه is a circumstantial phrase qualifying the blood, with the implied wording جاؤوا بدم كذب على قميصه.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r1.anchor: في محل نصب على الحال من " الدم ". قال أبو البقاء: " لأن التقدير: جاؤوا بدم كذب على قميصه

SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r2.claim: He rejects placing this circumstantial phrase before its governing genitive because a circumstantial phrase attached to a genitive cannot be advanced.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r2.anchor: فإن قلت: هل يجوز أن تكون حالا متقدمة؟ قلت: لا، لأن حال المجرور لا تتقدم عليه

SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r3.claim: The author says the restriction is only one grammatical view; a number of grammarians permit the advance and cite poetry.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r3.anchor: وهذا الذي رد به الزمخشري أحد قولي النحاة، وقد صحح جماعة جوازه وأنشدوا

SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r4.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r4.claim: He attaches على قميصه to جاؤوا, but the author objects that their arrival cannot meaningfully be on the shirt.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r4.anchor: وقال الحوفي: " إن " على قميصه " متعلق ب " جاؤوا " ، وفيه نظر؛ لأن مجيئهم لا يصح أن يكون على القميص

SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r5.claim: He treats على as an adverb meaning above, like arriving on camels with loads; the loads would be a circumstantial phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت " على قميصه " ما محله؟ قلت: محله النصب على الظرف، كأنه قيل

SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r6.claim: He objects that above cannot be an adverb for the people arriving; in the camel example it can describe the mounted traveler, with the loads as his state.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r6.anchor: ولا يساعد المعنى على نصب " على " على الظرف بمعنى فوق، لأن العامل فيه إذ ذاك " جاؤوا

SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r7.claim: The common كذب is a verbal noun used adjectivally for emphasis or means ذي كذب with an omitted noun, attributing the action to its doer.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r7.anchor: وقرأ العامة: " كذب " بالذال المعجمة، وهو من الوصف بالمصادر فيمكن أن يكون على سبيل المبالغة

SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r8.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r8.claim: He reads كذبا, which may be a causal object or a verbal noun functioning as a circumstantial qualifier, an uncommon use with an indefinite noun.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r8.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي " كذبا " فاحتمل أن يكون مفعولا من أجله واحتمل أن يكون مصدرا

SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r9.speaker: عائشة والحسن
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r9.claim: They read كدب with د; it can mean a mark like white spots in young people's nails, hence an effect on the shirt, or muddy, fresh, or dried blood.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18/r9.anchor: وقرأ عائشة والحسن: " كدب " بالدال المهملة. وقال صاحب اللوامح: " معناه: ذي كدب، أي: أثر

SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r1.claim: Before بل سولت an omitted denial is understood: the wolf did not eat him; سول means adorned or made easy.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r1.anchor:
قبل هذه الجملة جملة محذوفة تقديره: لم يأكله الذئب، بل سولت.
وسولت، أي: زينت وسهلت

SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r2.claim: فصبر جميل may be a subject with omitted predicate meaning a beautiful patience is best for me, or a predicate with omitted subject meaning my affair is beautiful patience.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r2.anchor: يجوز أن يكون مبتدأ وخبره محذوف، أي: صبر جميل أمثل بي. ويجوز أن يكون خبرا محذوف المبتدأ

SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r3.claim: Grammarians differ on whether the omitted subject or predicate is obligatory in this nominal construction; cited poetry also allows both parses.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r3.anchor: وضابطه أن يكون مصدرا في الأصل بدلا من اللفظ بفعله، وعبارة بعضهم تقتضي الوجوب

SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r4.speaker: أبي وعيسى بن عمر
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r4.claim: They read فصبرا جميلا in the accusative, also reported from al-Kisai and in Anas's codex; it may be a verbal noun, but imperative self-address is the stronger analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبي وعيسى بن عمر: " فصبرا جميلا " [نصبا، ورويت عن الكسائي، وكذلك هي في] مصحف أنس بن مالك

SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r5.claim: He calls the accusative reading weak if construed as a declarative verbal noun, since Sibawayh restricts that pattern to requests; he prefers an implied command to the self.
SAMIN-DURR:12:18#2/r5.anchor: وهذه قراءة ضعيفة إن خرجت هذا التخريج، فإن سيبويه لا ينقاس ذلك عنده إلا في الطلب

STUDYQURAN:12:18/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r1.claim: The brothers took Joseph's shirt after tearing it off before throwing him into the well; Genesis describes Jacob's special robe for Joseph.
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r1.anchor: The brothers had Joseph’s shirt from the moment they had torn it off him before they cast him into the well

STUDYQURAN:12:18/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r2.speaker: IṬ
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r2.claim: Before returning at night, the brothers stained the shirt with blood from a slaughtered baby goat or lamb.

STUDYQURAN:12:18/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r3.speaker: Aj, Ṭb
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r3.claim: Jacob's accusation means the brothers had persuaded themselves their deeds were not grievous, though he did not believe them.
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r3.anchor: they had convinced themselves that their actions were not grievous (Aj), but that he did not believe them (Ṭb)

STUDYQURAN:12:18/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r4.speaker: IṬ, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r4.claim: Jacob asks why the shirt showed no predator damage, since a wolf would have torn it apart while devouring Joseph.
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r4.anchor: if a wolf had devoured Joseph, his shirt would have been completely torn apart by the wolf (IṬ, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:12:18/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r5.claim: Beautiful patience means patience that complains to God alone; another reading is “My patience is/will be beautiful.” It consoles grief with hope that hardship passes and patience triumphs.
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r5.anchor: Beautiful patience! which refers to a kind of patience that causes one not to complain to anyone but God

STUDYQURAN:12:18/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r6.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r6.claim: Some interpret Jacob's words as “[My patience is/will be] a beautiful patience.”
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r6.anchor: Some interpret it to mean, “[My patience is/will be] a beautiful patience” (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:12:18/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r7.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r7.claim: Jacob says he seeks God's help to bear the lie his sons tell about Joseph's death; he repeats the words in verse 83.
STUDYQURAN:12:18/r7.anchor: means that Jacob seeks God’s Help in bearing the lie that his sons were telling him concerning Joseph’s death (Aj)

TAB-FULL:v13p38/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p38/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p38/r1.claim: Mujahid says the false blood came from a young sheep or goat, not Joseph.
TAB-FULL:v13p38/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {وجاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب} قال: دم سخلة "

TAB-FULL:v13p38/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p38/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p38/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reasons that a wolf would have torn the shirt if it had eaten Joseph, exposing the brothers’ story.
TAB-FULL:v13p38/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " {وجاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب} قال: لو أكله السبع لخرق القميص "

TAB-FULL:v13p38/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p38/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p38/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the brothers slaughtered a young goat, smeared its blood on the shirt, and brought it to Jacob.
TAB-FULL:v13p38/r3.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " ذبحوا جديا من الغنم، ثم لطخوا القميص بدمه، ثم أقبلوا إلى أبيهم

TAB-FULL:v13p38#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p38#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v13p38#2/r1.claim: Hasan reports that Jacob noticed blood but no tear and remarked that he had never known a wolf to be so gentle.
TAB-FULL:v13p38#2/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: " جيء بقميص يوسف إلى يعقوب، فجعل ينظر إليه فيرى أثر الدم، ولا يرى فيه خرقا،

TAB-FULL:v13p38#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p38#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p38#2/r2.claim: Qatada says Jacob found no mark of a predator, bite, or tear on the shirt; he also says the blood was not Joseph’s.
TAB-FULL:v13p38#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {وجاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب} قال: لما أتوا نبي الله يعقوب بقميصه،

TAB-FULL:v13p38#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p38#2/r3.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v13p38#2/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says the brothers killed a kid and stained the shirt; its intact condition showed Jacob they lied.
TAB-FULL:v13p38#2/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي، قال: " ذبحوا جديا ولطخوه من دمه؛ فلما نظر يعقوب إلى القميص صحيحا، عرف أن القوم كذبوه،

TAB-FULL:v13p39/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p39/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p39/r1.claim: A Basran grammarian treats كذب as describing the lie about the blood, like an expression in which a noun stands for an attributed quality.
TAB-FULL:v13p39/r1.anchor: أن يكون قيل {بدم كذب} [يوسف: 18] لأنه كذب فيه كما يقال: الليلة الهلال، وكما قيل: {فما ربحت تجارتهم} [البقرة: 16]

TAB-FULL:v13p39/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p39/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p39/r2.claim: A Kufan grammarian treats كذب as a verbal noun used for the passive participle: blood that was falsified or falsely attributed.
TAB-FULL:v13p39/r2.anchor: مصدر بمعنى مفعول، وتأويله: وجاءوا على قميصه بدم مكذوب، كما يقال: ما له عقل ولا معقول،

TAB-FULL:v13p39/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p39/r3.speaker: الراعي
TAB-FULL:v13p39/r3.claim: Al-Raʿi’s verse illustrates Arabic using a verbal noun where a passive participle is meant, with معقولا meaning something grasped or retained.
TAB-FULL:v13p39/r3.anchor: كما قال الراعي: [البحر الكامل] حتى إذا لم يتركوا لعظامه … لحما ولا لفؤاده معقولا

TAB-FULL:v13p39#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p39#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p39#2/r1.claim: Jacob rejects his sons’ account: their own selves made an act concerning Joseph seem attractive and good to them.
TAB-FULL:v13p39#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، " {قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا} [يوسف: 18] قال: يقول: بل زينت لكم أنفسكم أمرا "

TAB-FULL:v13p40/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r1.claim: Jacob calls his response to what his sons did beautiful patience and asks God to help him against the harm of their lies.
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {فصبر جميل} [يوسف: 18] قال: ليس فيه جزع "

TAB-FULL:v13p40/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r2.claim: Mujahid defines beautiful patience as patience without distress or complaint.
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {فصبر جميل} [يوسف: 18] قال: ليس فيه جزع "

TAB-FULL:v13p40/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r3.claim: A report attributes to the Prophet the definition of beautiful patience as patience without complaint, warning against broadcasting distress without patience.
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r3.anchor: عن حبان بن أبي جبلة، قال: " سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قوله: {فصبر جميل} [يوسف: 18] قال: «صبر لا شكوى فيه»

TAB-FULL:v13p40/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r4.speaker: الثوري
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r4.claim: Al-Thawri reports a saying that patience includes not voicing one’s pain or misfortune and not praising oneself.
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r4.anchor: عن بعض أصحابه قال: " يقال ثلاث من الصبر: أن لا تحدث بوجعك، ولا بمصيبتك، ولا تزكي نفسك "

TAB-FULL:v13p40/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r5.speaker: يعقوب
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r5.claim: A report says Jacob’s long sorrow led God to ask whether he was complaining of Him; Jacob answered that he had committed a sin and asked forgiveness.
TAB-FULL:v13p40/r5.anchor: عن حبيب بن أبي ثابت، " أن يعقوب النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم كان قد سقط حاجباه، فكان يرفعهما بخرقة،

TAB-FULL:v13p42/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p42/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p42/r1.claim: Qatada interprets Jacob’s appeal for God’s help against what his sons describe as help against their lies.
TAB-FULL:v13p42/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، " {والله المستعان على ما تصفون} [يوسف: 18] : أي على ما تكذبون "

ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r1.speaker: يروى
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r1.claim: A report says the brothers killed a young goat or ewe and smeared its blood on Joseph’s shirt after casting him into the well; both versions mean the same thing.
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r1.anchor:
يروى أنهم - رحمة " الله عليهم - لما طرحوا يوسف عليه السلام في
الجب أخذوا قميصه وذبحوا جديا فلطخوا القميص بدم الجدي.

ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r2.claim: Jacob replied that the brothers lied, since a wolf would have torn the shirt; another report has him remark that the wolf spared the shirt but ate his son.
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r2.anchor: فلما رأى يعقوب - صلى الله عليه وسلم - القميص قال: كذبتم، لو أكله الذئب لخرق قميصه.

ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r3.claim: دم كذب means fabricated blood, literally blood associated with a lie.
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r3.anchor: فالدم دم كذب، أي ذو كذب، والمعنى دم مكذوب

ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r4.claim: سولت لكم أنفسكم means your souls made an affair seem attractive to you.
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r4.anchor: أي بل زينت أنفسكم أمرا في قصة يوسف

ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r5.claim: Beautiful patience means enduring without panic or complaining to people.
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r5.anchor: معناه صبر لا جزع فيه ولا شكوى إلى الناس

ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r6.speaker: الخليل وجميع أصحابه
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r6.claim: The preferred nominative parse treats ‘beautiful patience’ as Jacob’s affair or settled conviction: ‘my affair is beautiful patience.’

ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r7.speaker: قطرب
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r7.claim: Qutrub parses it as ‘my patience is beautiful patience,’ supplying an omitted subject.
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r7.anchor: وهذا لفظ قطرب: فصبري صبر جميل.

ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r8.claim: Outside Qur’anic recitation, accusative صبرا جميلا is also possible, meaning ‘endure beautifully.’
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r8.anchor: وصبرا جميلا منصوب على مثل (فاصبر صبرا جميلا).

ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r9.speaker: منشدون
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r9.claim: Poetry uses صبر جميل as a nominative predicate, supporting the nominative construction.
ZAJJAJ:v3p96/r9.anchor:
وأنشدوا في الرفع:
شكا إلي جملي طول السرى. . . يا جملي ليس إلي المشتكى
صبر جميل

TABATABAI:12:17-18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r3.claim: The phrase “lying blood” uses the verbal noun as an emphatic active description, meaning blood that clearly lies about the alleged attack.
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r3.anchor: الكذب بالفتح فالكسر مصدر أريد به الفاعل للمبالغة أي بدم كاذب بين الكذب

TABATABAI:12:17-18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r4.claim: The indefinite, scant blood had little evidentiary force; an intact shirt contradicts their story because a devouring beast would have torn it.
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r4.anchor: فإن من افترسته السباع وأكلته لم تترك له قميصا سالما غير ممزق

TABATABAI:12:17-18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r5.claim: Deception cannot keep its credibility: contradictions within a lie or surrounding evidence eventually reveal it.
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r5.anchor: من المجرب أن الكذب لا يدوم على اعتباره وأن الكاذب لا يلبث دون أن يأتي بما يكذبه

TABATABAI:12:17-18/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r6.claim: Because events form an interconnected order of fixed relations and consequences, disguising one fact cannot conceal all its implications; truth ultimately prevails despite temporary falsehood.
TABATABAI:12:17-18/r6.anchor: أن الكون يجري على نظام يرتبط به بعض أجزائه ببعض بنسب وإضافات غير متغيرة ولا متبدلة

TABATABAI:12:18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:18/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:18/r1.claim: Jacob denies the wolf story: the brothers’ own selves had made some scheme attractive to them, and his unspecific wording both accuses and avoids naming their deed.
TABATABAI:12:18/r1.anchor: والتسويل الوسوسة أي ليس الأمر على ما تخبرون بل وسوست لكم أنفسكم فيه أمرا

TABATABAI:12:18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:18/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:18/r2.claim: “Beautiful patience” praises patience by naming the cause for its result; its indefinite form and omitted adjective suggest either its grandeur or its bitterness and difficulty.
TABATABAI:12:18/r2.anchor: وقوله { فصبر جميل } مدح للصبر وهو من قبيل وضع السبب موضع المسبب

TABATABAI:12:18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:18/r3.claim: The circumstances leave Jacob with no practical path but patience: his beloved son is said to be dead, he sees the brothers’ lie, and his only powerful helpers are the suspected perpetrators.

TABATABAI:12:18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:18/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:18/r4.claim: Patience is not passive submission to abuse; it is inner steadiness and clear judgment, while people remain properly equipped to resist harm as far as they can.
TABATABAI:12:18/r4.anchor: بل الصبر هو الاستقامة في القلب وحفظ النظام النفساني الذي به يستقيم أمر الحياة الإنسانية من الاختلال

TABATABAI:12:18#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r1.claim: The patient remain upright under calamity rather than fleeing at its first assault; patience protects inner order and sound deliberation.
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r1.anchor: فالصابرون هم القائمون في النوائب على ساق لا تزيلهم هجمات المكاره

TABATABAI:12:18#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r2.claim: Patience is a defensive fortress, but recovery needs a further cause; in monotheism that cause is God, so one first preserves inner devotion and then entrusts the outcome to Him.
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r2.anchor: وهذا السبب في ملة التوحيد هو الله عز سلطانه فعلى الإنسان الموحد إذا نابته نائبة ونزلت عليه مصيبة أن يتحصن أولا بالصبر

TABATABAI:12:18#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r3.claim: Jacob completes patience with trust in God, just as he later says he hopes God will bring his sons back together.
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r3.anchor: ولهذا كله لما قال يعقوب عليه السلام { فصبر جميل } عقبه بقوله { والله المستعان على ما تصفون }

TABATABAI:12:18#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r4.claim: Jacob knows the brothers plotted and that the wolf story is false, yet asks God alone to expose their claim and restore Joseph rather than relying on outward causes independently.
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r4.anchor: أني أعلم أن لكم في الأمر مكرا وأن يوسف لم يأكله ذئب لكنى لا أركن في كشف كذبكم

TABATABAI:12:18#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r5.claim: “God is the one sought for help” is a prayer expressing exclusive divine agency: Jacob omits himself and submits the matter to God’s rightful rule.
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r5.anchor: والكلمة مبنية على توحيد الفعل فإنها مسوقة سوق الحصر ومعناها أن الله سبحانه هو المستعان

TABATABAI:12:18#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r6.claim: Even in grief, Jacob’s love for Joseph and sorrow at losing him are wholly for God’s sake, not self-centered attachment.
TABATABAI:12:18#2/r6.anchor: غير أنه ما كان يحب يوسف ولا يتوله فيه ولا يجد لفقده إلا لله وفي الله

TABATABAI:12:7-21#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:7-21#4/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:7-21#4/r5.claim: A report attributed through Abu al-Jarud says the brothers slaughtered a young goat on Joseph’s shirt to make the bloodstain.
TABATABAI:12:7-21#4/r5.anchor: وفيه وفي رواية أبي الجارود في قول الله { وجاؤا على قميصه بدم كذب } قال إنهم ذبحوا جديا

TABATABAI:12:7-21#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:7-21#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:7-21#4/r6.claim: Al-Tusi’s report glosses beautiful patience as patience without complaint; Tabatabai guesses it comes from al-Sadiq and notes a similar Prophetic report from Hayyan ibn Jabala.
TABATABAI:12:7-21#4/r6.anchor: وفي أمالي الشيخ بإسناده في قوله عز وجل { فصبر جميل } قال بلا شكوى

TABRISI:12:13-18/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:13-18/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:13-18/r4.claim: The phrase dam kadhib may mean blood falsely attributed to Joseph, or be parsed as a verbal noun meaning “falsified”; al-Farrāʾ accepts a verbal noun for the passive sense, but Sībawayh rejects that analysis and offers an alternative ellipsis. ʿĀʾisha’s reading kadb with dāl means fresh blood.
TABRISI:12:13-18/r4.anchor: ودم كذب أي مكذوب فيه وهو مصدر وصف به. وقيل: إن تقديره بدم ذي كذب

TABRISI:12:16-18/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:16-18/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:16-18/r2.claim: “Beautiful patience” may predicate an omitted “my affair” or “my patience,” or be a subject with an omitted predicate; a non-Qurʾānic accusative is also reported as an exhortation to the self, with poetic parallels.
TABRISI:12:16-18/r2.anchor: وصبر جميل مرفوع على أحد وجهين على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف وتقديره فشأني صبر جميل

TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid say the brothers killed a young sheep and smeared Joseph’s shirt with its blood; another account says it was a deer. They failed to notice that a wolf would tear the shirt.
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: إنهم ذبحوا سخلة وجعلوا دمها على قميصه عن ابن عباس ومجاهد. وقيل: ظبيا

TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Jacob asked to see the intact shirt and remarked that he had never known such a gentle wolf, which ate his son without tearing the garment; another report has him cover his face and call it a merciful wolf.
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r7.anchor: عن الحسن وروي أنه ألقى ثوبه على وجهه وقال يا يوسف لقد أكلك ذئب رحيم

TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r8.claim: Dam kadhib means blood falsely attributed or falsified, like “poured water” meaning water that was poured out.
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r8.anchor: مكذوب عليه أوفيه كما يقال ماء سكب أي مسكوب وشراب صب أي مصبوب

TABRISI:12:18/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
