TABRISI:12:18/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:18/r1.claim: The cited poem uses a lament image: the horses remain mourning for the dead, with reins drooping in grief.
TABRISI:12:18/r1.anchor: تظل جيادهم نوحا عليهم مقلدة أعنتها صفونا أراد نائحة عليهم

TABRISI:12:18/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:18/r2.speaker: الشعبي
TABRISI:12:18/r2.claim: Joseph's shirt bore three signs: it was torn from behind, later restored Jacob's sight, and its undamaged state exposed the false blood story because a wolf would have torn it.
TABRISI:12:18/r2.anchor: حين قد من دبر وحين ألقي على وجه أبيه فارتد بصيرا وحين جاؤوا عليه بدم كذب

TABRISI:12:18/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:18/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:18/r3.claim: When the brothers blamed thieves, Jacob asked how they could have killed Joseph yet left the shirt, which they needed more than his death.
TABRISI:12:18/r3.anchor: فكيف قتلوه وتركوا قميصه وهم إلى قميصه أحوج منهم إلى قتله

TABRISI:12:18/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:18/r4.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:12:18/r4.claim: Jacob said the wolf and thieves were not responsible; their own selves had embellished a deed they knew about.
TABRISI:12:18/r4.anchor: زينت لكم أنفسكم أمرا علمتموه عن قتادة

TABRISI:12:18/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:18/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم والجبائي
TABRISI:12:18/r5.claim: They explain that the brothers made the crime easy for one another until they killed Joseph.
TABRISI:12:18/r5.anchor: سهل بعضكم لبعض أمرا في يوسف غير الذي فعلتموه حتى سهل عليكم فقتلتموه عن أبي مسلم والجبائي

TABRISI:12:18/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:18/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:18/r6.claim: One view says Jacob accused them by revelation from God; another says he inferred the truth through sound judgment and a clear mind.
TABRISI:12:18/r6.anchor: رد يعقوب عليهم بوحي من الله عز اسمه

TABRISI:12:18/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:18/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:18/r7.claim: Beautiful patience means enduring without agitation or complaining to people.
TABRISI:12:18/r7.anchor: فصبري صبر جميل لا جزع فيه ولا شكوى إلى الناس

TABRISI:12:18/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:18/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:18/r8.claim: Another explanation calls beautiful patience better and more fitting than useless agitation.
TABRISI:12:18/r8.anchor: فصبر جميل أحسن وأولى من الجزع الذي لا يغني شيئا

TABRISI:12:18/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:18/r9.speaker: المرتضى
TABRISI:12:18/r9.claim: Patience is beautiful when undertaken for God's sake and in the way one is obligated to endure; Jacob's patience met that standard.
TABRISI:12:18/r9.anchor: إنما يكون الصبر جميلا إذا قصد به وجه الله تعالى وفعل للوجه الذي وجب

TABRISI:12:18/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:18/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:18/r10.claim: Jacob and the blameless young Joseph were tested through grief and enslavement under God's watch until relief came.
TABRISI:12:18/r10.anchor: البلاء نزل بيعقوب على كبره وبيوسف على صغره بلا ذنب كان منهما

TABRISI:12:18/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:18/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:18/r11.claim: Jacob seeks God's help either to resist the brothers' account or to bear the bitter patience it requires; Joseph stayed in the well three days.
TABRISI:12:18/r11.anchor: بالله أستعين على دفع ما تصفون أو به أستعين على تحمل مرارة الصبر عليه ومكث يوسف في الجب ثلاثة أيام

THALABI:v5p202/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p202/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p202/r5.claim: The blood on the shirt was false because it was sheep’s blood, not Joseph’s; alternatively the phrase means blood that was lied about or ‘a blood of lying.’
THALABI:v5p202/r5.anchor: وجاؤ على قميصه بدم كذب أي بدم كذب

THALABI:v5p202/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p202/r6.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v5p202/r6.claim: Aisha read كدب with a dal, meaning fresh blood.
THALABI:v5p202/r6.anchor: وقرأت عائشة: بدم كدب بالدال غير المعجمة، أي طري

THALABI:v5p202/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p202/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p202/r7.claim: Jacob points out that the wolf supposedly ate Joseph without tearing his shirt, calling it a remarkably judicious wolf.
THALABI:v5p202/r7.anchor: فقال: يا لله ما رأيت كاليوم ذئبا أحلم من هذا

THALABI:v5p202/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p202/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p202/r8.claim: بل سولت لكم means the brothers’ own selves arranged a plan; فصبر جميل may mean my state or act is beautiful patience, or simply ‘my patience is beautiful.’
THALABI:v5p202/r8.anchor: فحينئذ قال بل سولت لكم أنفسكم رتبت لكم أمرا فصبر أي فمني أو فعلي صبر

THALABI:v5p202/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p202/r9.speaker: الأشهب والعقيلي
THALABI:v5p202/r9.claim: Al-Ashhab and al-Uqayli read فصبرا as an accusative verbal noun, meaning ‘I will be patient’ with no lament or complaint.
THALABI:v5p202/r9.anchor: وقرأ الأشهب والعقيلي: فصبرا على المصدر أي فلأصبرن صبرا جميلا

THALABI:v5p202/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p202/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p202/r10.claim: Another interpretation is that Jacob will continue to deal with his sons graciously rather than in a mournful, grieving manner.
THALABI:v5p202/r10.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا أعاشركم على كآبة الوجه وحبوس الحنين، بل أكون في المعاشرة

THALABI:v5p202/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p202/r11.speaker: حبيب بن ثابت
THALABI:v5p202/r11.claim: A report says Jacob’s brows drooped over his eyes from long years and sorrow; God asked if he complained of Him, and Jacob asked forgiveness for a sin.
THALABI:v5p202/r11.anchor: وروى عبد الرزاق عن الثوري عن حبيب بن ثابت أن يعقوب النبي (عليه السلام) كان قد سقط

THALABI:v5p203/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p203/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p203/r1.claim: Jacob says God is the help against the brothers’ false account; reports place Joseph’s age when thrown in the well at eighteen, seventeen, or ten, and his stay there at three days.
THALABI:v5p203/r1.anchor: والله المستعان على ما تصفون من الكذب، قالوا: وكان يوسف حين ألقي في الجب ابن ثماني عشرة سنة

ASAD-NOTES:12:16#n18/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:16#n18/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:16#n18/r1.claim: Jacob’s words literally mean that he turns to God for aid against the misfortune his sons described.
ASAD-NOTES:12:16#n18/r1.anchor: it is to God that I turn for aid against what you are describing

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r1.speaker: ابن عباس؛ مجاهد؛ عامة المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r1.claim: The blood on Joseph’s shirt was from a slaughtered lamb; other reports suggest a kid goat or camel calf.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r2.speaker: الفراء؛ أبو العباس؛ الزجاج؛ ابن الأنباري؛ الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r2.claim: Bi-damin kadhib means blood falsely claimed to be Joseph’s; the verbal noun kadhib describes the object for emphasis, as in “unprofitable trade” and other source-noun adjectives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r2.anchor: أي مكذوب فيه، إلا أنه وصف بالمصدر على تقدير: ذي كذب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r3.speaker: الحسن؛ سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r3.claim: Jacob calls the story a lie: a wolf would not have eaten his son without tearing the shirt.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r4.speaker: الكلبي عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r4.claim: In another account Jacob says the wolf was unusually gentle; when the brothers blame robbers, he asks why they left the shirt, which they needed more than the killing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p46/r4.anchor: لقد كان هذا الذئب رفيقا حين أكل ابني ولم يخرق قميصه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r1.speaker: ابن عباس؛ عامة المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r1.claim: Sawwalat means their selves adorned or made the deed seem attractive to them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني؛ الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r2.claim: Taswīl is forming a hoped-for wish in the soul; al-Azharī relates it to a desired ambition that beautifies falsehood and worldly aims, with hamza softened because frequent use made it burdensome.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r2.anchor: التسويل تقدير معنى في النفس على الطمع في

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r3.claim: Bal rejects the brothers’ wolf account and replaces it with the charge that their own selves devised another matter.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r4.speaker: مجاهد؛ المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r4.claim: Beautiful patience means enduring without despair or complaint; a Prophetic report defines it as patience without complaint, with no grading stated.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r5.claim: Beautiful patience shows no visible change, such as a frown or withdrawal from one’s former openness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r5.anchor: أن يصبر حتى لا يظهر فيه تغير بعبوس وجه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r6.speaker: الخليل؛ قطرب؛ الفراء؛ أبو عبيد؛ الزجاج؛ ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r6.claim: They supply different implied predicates for the nominative ṣabrun: what I believe, my patience, it is, let it be mine, my affair, or equivalent meanings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r6.anchor: فقال الخليل (¬6): معناه: فالذي أعتقده صبر جميل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق؛ أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r7.claim: Outside Qurʾānic wording, ṣabran jamīlan is possible; raising is preferable when patience is described, while accusative suits an indefinite standalone noun, with poetry illustrating the accusative.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r7.anchor: ويجوز في غير القرآن: فصبرا جميلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r8.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r8.claim: Appealing to God for help expresses the piety that calls for beautiful patience and reliance on God amid terrible events.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p48/r8.anchor: هذا بيان عما يوجبه التقى من الصبر الجميل عند المصيبة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:17-20/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:17-20/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:17-20/r2.claim: The blood on Joseph’s shirt was false: it was the blood of a young goat, not his own.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:17-20/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:17-20/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:17-20/r3.claim: Jacob says their souls embellished another affair about Joseph; his beautiful patience contains no anguished complaint, and God is his aid in enduring their account.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:17-20/r3.anchor: وهو الذي لا جزع فيه ولا شكوى

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:16/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:16/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:16/r3.claim: Jacob’s remark showed that he did not believe his sons; he then stated his suspicion directly by saying their own selves had led them into an evil deed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:16/r3.anchor: Ya‘kūb bu sözleriyle oğullarının söylediklerine inanmadığını ifade etmek istemiştir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Sawwalat means Satan made something seem attractive, easy, and acceptable to a person.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Satan seem a certain thing seem fair to them as well as very acceptable too

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: For “beautiful patience,” Islahi prefers treating the phrase as an inchoative with its predicate suppressed; an alternative makes it the predicate of a suppressed inchoative, and suppression focuses attention.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: I have preferred the first of these.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Beautiful patience is free of complaint, grumbling, and wailing.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This patience referred to is one that does not have any element of complaint, grumbling and wailing in it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur’anic account contrasts Jacob's graceful patience with the Torah's depiction of him tearing his clothes, wearing sackcloth, and mourning for many days.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Then Jacob tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and mourned for his son many days

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the blood smeared on Joseph’s shirt was from a lamb or young goat.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#2/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس ﴿ وجاؤوا على قميصه بدم كذب ﴾ قال دم سخلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r1.claim: Reported age estimates give Joseph as seven or six, while Hasan is cited for twelve or eighteen and Ibn al-Sa'ib for seventeen; Abu Hayyan regards the older estimates as unlikely.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r1.anchor: فقيل: كان عمره إذ ذاك سبع سنين. وقيل: ست، قاله الضحاك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan concludes Joseph was a young child, likely seven: Jacob feared a wolf, the brothers expected him to play, a passerby called him a boy, and the Egyptian hoped to adopt him; reports of ages 12 to 18 are unlikely.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r5.anchor: والذي يظهر من سياق الأخبار والقصص أن يوسف كان صغيرا، فقيل: كان عمره إذ ذاك سبع سنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r7.claim: A report says they slaughtered a young sheep or goat, stained Joseph's shirt, and presented it; Jacob saw no tear and challenged the idea of a wolf gentle enough to eat him without damaging his shirt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r7.anchor: روي أنهم أخذوا سخلة أو جديا فذبحوه، ولطخوا قميص يوسف بدمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r1.claim: One account gives Joseph's shirt three signs: it showed the wolf had not eaten him, later restored Jacob's sight, and proved Joseph's innocence when his back was torn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r1.anchor: قيل: كان في قميص يوسف ثلاث آيات، كان دليلا ليعقوب على أن يوسف لم يأكله الذئب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari construes 'on his shirt' as an adverb meaning over it, and rejects an early circumstantial phrase from a prepositional complement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r2.anchor: محله النصب على الظرف، كأنه قيل: وجاؤوا فوق قميصه بدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that 'over the shirt' cannot be an adverb of the arriving brothers; he also finds al-Hawfi's direct attachment unsuitable, while al-Baqa' treats it as a state of the blood, an analysis supported by the sense despite grammatical disagreement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r3.anchor: ولا يساعد المعنى على نصب على على الظرف بمعنى فوق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r4.claim: The majority read 'lying' as an emphatic adjective for blood, or understand 'blood of a lie' with an omitted noun, since the blood itself manifests their lie.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: كذب وصف لدم على سبيل المبالغة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads 'a lie' in the accusative, either as a circumstantial verbal noun or causal object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r5.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: كذبا بالنصب، فاحتمل أن يكون مصدرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r6.speaker: عائشة والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r6.claim: Aisha and Hasan read the word with dāl; glosses include murky, fresh, dry, or a mark of white on young men's nails, metaphorically describing the stain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r6.anchor: وقرأت عائشة، والحسن: كدب بالدال غير معجمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r7.claim: With an omitted 'the wolf did not eat him,' Ibn Abbas glosses 'your souls enticed you' as 'I commanded you to do something'; Qatada says they adorned it, and others say they approved or eased an ugly deed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p250/r7.anchor: قال: بل سولت هنا محذوف تقديره: لم يأكله الذئب، بل سولت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r1.claim: 'So beautiful patience' may omit 'my affair is' or mean patience is best; Ubayy, al-Ashhab, and Isa ibn Umar read both words accusative, as do two codices and a report from al-Kisa'i.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r1.anchor: فأمري صبر جميل، أو فصبر جميل أمثل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r2.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r2.claim: Sibawayh considers the accusative reading weak unless construed as a command to the self, like a poetic imperative to endure beautifully.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r2.anchor: قيل: وهي قراءة ضعيفة عند سيبويه، ولا يصلح النصب في مثل هذا إلا مع الأمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r3.claim: A hadith defines beautiful patience as having no complaint to people; Jacob's later statement that he complains only to God is cited in support.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث: «أن الصبر الجميل أنه الذي لا شكوى فيه»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that Jacob keeps a composed face and continues associating with his family as before; al-Thawri says patience means not recounting what hurts, one's calamity, or self-pity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r4.anchor: وقيل: أتجمل لكم في صبري فلا أعاشركم على كآبة الوجه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r5.claim: God is the one from whom Jacob seeks help in bearing the alleged loss and enduring the calamity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p251/r5.anchor: والله المستعان أي: المطلوب منه العون على احتمال ما تصفون

ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r1.claim: دم كذب means blood characterized by falsehood, as though it were falsehood itself; the source also allows the passive sense blood falsely alleged to be Joseph's.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r1.anchor: أي ذي كذب أو وصف بالمصدر مبالغة كأنه نفس الكذب وعينه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r2.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī's accusative كذبا is parsed as a circumstantial accusative from the brothers, meaning they came lying; it may instead qualify the blood or be causal, though a circumstantial from an indefinite noun is disfavored.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r2.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما كذبا بالنصب وخرج على أنه في موضع الحال

ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r3.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r3.claim: ʿĀʾisha and al-Ḥasan are reported to read كَدِب with dāl; it is a separate lexical form meaning muddy, fresh, or dry, and can therefore express opposite senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r3.anchor: وقرأت عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها والحسن كدب بالدال المهملة وليس من قلب الذال

ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r4.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r4.claim: The source of al-Lawāmiʿ explains the dāl form as having a trace or mark, like the white spots that appear in young men's nails.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r4.anchor: وقال صاحب اللوامح : المعنى ذي كدب أي أثر لأن الكدب بياض

ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r5.claim: Some grammarians treat the blood as a vivid simile for a false mark on the shirt, without an omitted possessive modifier.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r5.anchor: ولم يعتبر بعض المحققين تقدير المضاف وجعل ذلك من التشبيه البليغ أو الإستعارة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r6.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ takes على قميصه as a circumstantial phrase modifying the blood; grammarians dispute whether a circumstantial can precede a genitive governed by a preposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200/r6.anchor: وقوله سبحانه : ( على قميصه ) على ما ذهب إليه أبو البقاء حال من دم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r1.claim: On the preferred construal, the brothers came with false blood placed above Joseph's shirt; other grammatical accounts make them arrive possessing the shirt, with the blood as a circumstance, but the difference is minor.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r1.anchor: والمعنى أتوا بدم كذب فوق قميصه ولا يخفى إستقامته

ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid report that the brothers slaughtered a lamb and smeared its blood on Joseph's shirt.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r2.anchor: لطخوا بدمها القميص كما روي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r3.claim: Qatāda's report says they instead killed a gazelle and smeared its blood on the shirt; Jacob found no tooth or claw marks and called the wolf unusually merciful.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ عن قتادة أنهم أخذوا ظبيا فذبحوه فلطخوا بدمه القميص

ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r4.claim: Further reports describe Jacob kissing the shirt and weeping until his face was stained, or collapsing unconscious; Judah checked for breath, lamented that they had lost their brother and father, and Jacob revived near dawn.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r4.anchor: وفي رواية أنه أخذ القميص وألقاه على وجهه وبكى حتى خضب وجهه بدم القميص

ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r5.claim: سولت لكم means that their selves made an evil deed seem attractive and easy; al-Rāghib defines it as painting what one desires in the mind as beautiful.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p200#2/r5.anchor: وقال الراغب : هو تزيين النفس لما تحرص عليه وتصوير القبيح بصورة الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r1.speaker: الأزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r1.claim: Al-Azharī derives تسويل from the person's desire or wish, which beautifies falsehood to the one pursuing it; a less likely derivation links it to laxity of the nerves.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r1.anchor: وقال الأزهري : كأن التسويل تفعيل من سوال الإنسان وهو أمنيته

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r2.claim: Jacob knew the story was false because Joseph's shirt was intact; the shirt is also linked to his restored sight and to Joseph's innocence when it was torn from behind.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r2.anchor: وعلمه عليه السلام بكذبهم قيل : حصل من سلامة القميص عن التمزيق

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r3.claim: Another explanation is that Jacob exposed their inconsistencies: after asking why a wolf left the shirt intact, one brother blamed robbers, prompting Jacob to ask why robbers would leave the shirt they needed more than the killing.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r3.anchor: وقيل : من تناقضهم فإنه يروى أنه عليه السلام لما قال

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r4.claim: Even knowing they lied, Jacob grieved because he feared Joseph's suffering, or because separation from loved ones is unbearable; the author allows both fear and separation as causes.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r4.anchor: ولعله مع هذا العلم إنما حزن عليه السلام لما خشي عليه من المكروه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r5.speaker: قطرب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r5.claim: One ellipsis supplies my affair or my patience as the subject of فصبر جميل.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r5.anchor: أي فأمري صبر جميل أو فصبري صبر جميل كما قال قطرب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r6.speaker: الخليل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r6.claim: Al-Khalīl supplies a verbal sense: what I will do is that; other analyses understand the phrase as an omitted subject and predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r6.anchor: أو فالذي أفعله ذلك كما قال الخليل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r7.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ construes the phrase as an omitted nominal clause meaning it is beautiful patience.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r7.anchor: أو فهو صبر الخ كما قال الفراء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r8.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r8.claim: Ubayy, al-Ashhab, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, as well as a copy attributed to Anas, read both words in the accusative, parsed as an imperative to be patient.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبي والأشهب وعيسى بن عمر فصبرا جميلا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r9.claim: The accusative reading is challenged because the form usually requires an imperative; one reply has Jacob address himself: O soul, be patient with beautiful patience.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r9.anchor: وتعقب بأنه لا يحسن النصب في مثل ذلك إلا مع الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r10.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r10.claim: A Prophetic report attributed to al-Ḥasan defines beautiful patience as patience without complaint to people; the later appeal to God is not excluded.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r10.anchor: والصبر الجميل على ما روى الحسن عنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ما لا شكوى فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r11.claim: A report says Jacob's brows fell over his eyes and he raised them with a bandage; asked why, he cited time and grief, then God asked whether he was complaining to anyone but Him, and Jacob sought forgiveness.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201/r11.anchor: وقيل : إنه عليه السلام سقط حاجباه على عينيه فكان برفعهما بعصابة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r1.claim: God is the one from whom Jacob continually seeks help; he asks God to expose their lie by preserving Joseph and restoring their reunion, parallel to his later hope that God will bring them all back.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r1.anchor: ومعنى استعانته عليه السلام بالله تعالى على كذبهم طلبه منه سبحانه إظهار كونه كذبا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r2.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r2.claim: During the slander incident, ʿĀʾisha said her accusers would not believe an oath or accept an excuse and compared herself to Jacob's sons, then invoked God's help; revelation declared her innocence.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r2.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت يوم الإفك : والله لئن حلفت

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r3.claim: Another reading asks God to help Jacob bear the claim that Joseph is dead, or to bear the strain of resisting grief; the two clauses parallel worship and reliance in the opening of al-Fātiḥa.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r3.anchor: فقوله : ( فصبر جميل ) يجري مجرى ( إياك نعبد )

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r4.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī objects that patiently accepting oppression is not obligatory: Jacob should have investigated, rescued Joseph if alive, or sought retribution if murdered, especially since revelation and his standing suggested Joseph survived.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r4.anchor: للإمام الرازي عليه الرحمة في هذا المقام بحث وهو : أن الصبر على قضاء الله تعالى واجب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r5.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r5.claim: The reported replies are that God forbade investigation to intensify the trial; the sons could have prevented it or harmed Jacob; Jacob knew God would protect and exalt Joseph; he wished not to disgrace his sons; or the harm could not yet be undone.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r5.anchor: ثم قال : والجواب أن نقول : لا جواب عن ذلك إلا أن يقال

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r6.claim: The parental dilemma is illustrated by a poet: punishing one son for harming another wounds the father, while pardoning or striking both also causes pain.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r6.anchor: ونظير ذلك ما أشار إليه الشاعر بقوله : قومي هم قتلوا أميم أخي فإذا رميت

ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r7.claim: The interpretation that Jacob promised to conceal his displeasure and keep a cheerful face among his sons is very far from the apparent meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p201#2/r7.anchor: أنى أتجعل لكم في صبري فلا أعاشركم على كآبة الوجه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r1.claim: The blood on the shirt was false because it was not Yusuf's blood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r1.anchor: بدم هو كذب، لأنه لم يكن دم يوسف.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r2.claim: An alternative parses the blood as fabricated, with the verbal noun standing in for a noun.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r2.anchor: بدم مكذوب فيه، فوضع المصدر موضع الاسم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r3.claim: In the narrative, the brothers stained the shirt without tearing it, so Yaqub suspected them because a wolf would have torn it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r3.anchor: لطخوا القميص بالدم ولم يشقوه، فقال يعقوب عليه السلام: كيف أكله الذئب ولم يشق قميصه؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r4.claim: Sawwalat means that their selves adorned or made their story seem attractive to them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r5.claim: Beautiful patience means either that his affair or conduct is beautiful patience.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r5.anchor: معناه: فأمري صبر جميل أو فعلي صبر جميل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r6.claim: An alternative takes the phrase as Yaqub choosing beautiful patience.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r7.claim: Beautiful patience has neither complaint nor despair.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r7.anchor: والصبر الجميل الذي لا شكوى فيه ولا جزع.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r8.claim: Yaqub seeks God's help to endure what they describe falsely.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r8.anchor: أستعين بالله على الصبر، على ما تكذبون.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r9.claim: The brothers brought a wolf and claimed it had eaten Yusuf; God made it speak, and it said it had never seen his face.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r9.anchor: فقال له يعقوب: يا ذئب أنت أكلت ولدي وثمرة فؤادي؟ فأنطقه الله عز وجل، فقال: تالله ما رأيت وجه ابنك قط.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r10.claim: In the story, the wolf said it had come to visit kin, but the brothers captured it.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r11.claim: The narrative says Yusuf remained in the well for three days.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222#2/r11.anchor: فمكث يوسف في البئر ثلاثة أيام

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r1.claim: Dam kadhib means blood bearing a lie, or a source used adjectivally for emphasis; the accusative reading makes it circumstantial, and kadib without dots can mean murky or fresh.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r1.anchor: أي ذي كذب بمعنى مكذوب فيه، ويجوز أن يكون وصفا بالمصدر للمبالغة وقرىء بالنصب على الحال من الواو

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r2.claim: Another view compares the blood to the white substance on young people's nails; ʿalā qamīṣihi may mean above the shirt or describe the blood despite its fronted position.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r2.anchor: وقيل: أصله البياض الخارج على أظفار الأحداث فشبه به الدم اللاصق على القميص

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r3.claim: A report says Jacob took the shirt, wept until it stained his face, and called the wolf patient for not tearing it; he asks God for help, and the source says this crime predated prophethood if true.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r3.anchor: روي: أنه لما سمع بخبر يوسف صاح وسأل عن قميصه فأخذه وألقاه على وجهه وبكى حتى خضب وجهه

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r4.claim: Sawwalt means their selves made a grave deed seem easy and attractive; the root suggests slackness; beautiful patience is either Jacob's affair or the best patience.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r4.anchor: أي سهلت لكم أنفسكم وهونت في أعينكم أمرا عظيما من السول وهو الاسترخاء. { فصبر جميل } أي فأمري صبر جميل

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r5.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r5.claim: The Prophet defines beautiful patience as not complaining to people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:18-19/r5.anchor: الصبر الجميل الذي لا شكوى فيه إلى الخلق

BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r5.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the brothers slaughtered a young ewe and smeared its blood on Joseph's shirt as fabricated evidence.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r5.anchor: نقله الرماني عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وعن مجاهد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r6.speaker: مجاهد
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r6.claim: Mujahid is also cited for the account that the brothers used a slaughtered ewe's blood to falsify Joseph's death.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وعن مجاهد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r7.claim: The blood is called a lie because their claim that it was Joseph's blood contradicted reality; blood is a red, flowing substance normally found in animal veins.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r7.anchor: أي مكذوب , أطلق عليه المصدر مبالغة لأنه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r8.claim: An unattributed report says Jacob threw the shirt over his face and cried until its blood stained him, remarking that he had never seen such a gentle wolf.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r8.anchor: وروي أن يعقوب عليه الصلاة والسلام أخذ القميص منهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r9.claim: The shirt serves as three signs: proof the brothers lied, proof Joseph was truthful when his shirt was torn from behind, and a means by which his father's sight returned.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r9.anchor: وكان القميص ثلاث آيات : دلالته على كذبهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r10.claim: Jacob did not press them for Joseph's remains: a wolf normally leaves some prey, but asking could provoke worse harm; his later instruction to search for Joseph supports this.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r10.anchor: من الشرور أكثر مما جاؤوا به من المحذور

BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r1.claim: Jacob says their souls embellished and made their deed seem easy; beautiful patience means enduring without complaining to people, while God is the one asked for help against their account.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r1.anchor: أي زينت وسهلت , من السول وهو الاسترخاء

BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r2.claim: The brothers are not thereby hypocrites: breaking promises, lying, and betraying trust occurred once, whereas hypocrisy makes them habitual or predominant.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r2.anchor: ولا يقال : إنهم بهذا أجمعوا أوصاف المنافق ( إذا وعد أخلف

BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r3.claim: The lexical permutations of sawl and sayl cluster around desired aims and their attendant senses, including longing, adornment, ease, deception, treatment, persistence, comfort, and hardship.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r3.anchor: تدوران على ما يطمع فيه من المراد , ويلزمه رغد العيش والزينة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r4.speaker: القزاز
BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r4.claim: Al-Qazzaz says wasila can mean rank or position with a king; the passage also gives it the senses of a need and seeking access.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p18/r4.anchor: قال القزاز : وقيل : توسلت وتوصلت - بمعنى , والوسيلة : الحاجة

DURR-FULL:v4p513/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r1.claim: ‘Your souls made this seem good’ means they embellished the matter for themselves; ‘beautiful patience’ means patience regarding what they claim falsely.
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r1.anchor:
عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا}
يقول: بل زينت لكم أنفسكم أمرا

DURR-FULL:v4p513/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r2.speaker: حيان بن أبي حيلة
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r2.claim: The Prophet defines beautiful patience as having no complaint of distress; whoever complained did not remain patient.
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r2.anchor: عن حيان بن أبي حيلة رضي الله عنه قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن قوله {فصبر جميل

DURR-FULL:v4p513/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r3.claim: Beautiful patience contains no agitation or despair.
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {فصبر جميل} قال: ليس فيه جزع

DURR-FULL:v4p513/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r4.claim: Beautiful patience includes complaint only to God.
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r4.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: الصبر الجميل الذي ليس فيه شكوى إلا إلى الله

DURR-FULL:v4p513/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r5.speaker: الثوري عن بعض الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r5.claim: Three forms of patience are not speaking about what hurts or one’s calamity, and not praising oneself.
DURR-FULL:v4p513/r5.anchor: عن الثوري عن بعض الصحابة قال: يقال ثلاثة من الصبر: أن لا تحدث بما يوجعك

ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r2.claim: Beautiful patience is inner and outward stillness before divine decree.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r2.anchor: وهو السكون إلى موارد القضاء سرا وعلنا

ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r3.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r3.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh defines it as meeting affliction with open heart and cheerful face.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r3.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ : الصبر الجميل أن يتلقى البلاء بقلب رحيب ووجه مستبشر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r4.speaker: الترمذي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r4.claim: Al-Tirmidhī says it is handing oneself to the Lord with true knowledge and accepting His decree without distress.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r4.anchor: وقال الترمذي : هو أن يلقى العبد عنانه إلى مولاه ويسلم اليه نفسه مع حقيقة المعرفة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r5.speaker: الشبلي
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r5.claim: Al-Shiblī’s poem depicts the sufferer calling to patience itself to endure.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r5.anchor: وأنشد الشبلي في حقيقة الصبر + عبرات خططن في الخد سطرا

DURR-FULL:v4p501/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p501/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v4p501/r8.claim: The brothers killed a goat, smeared its blood on Joseph's shirt, and claimed a wolf had eaten him. Jacob inferred that the wolf was merciful because it had not torn the shirt.
DURR-FULL:v4p501/r8.anchor: فأخذوا جديا من الغنم فذبحوه ونضحوا دمه على القميص ثم أقبلوا إلى أبيهم عشاء يبكون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r1.claim: “Your souls made it seem good” means they adorned another account for you.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r1.anchor: أي زينت ( لكم أنفسكم أمرا ) غير ما تصفون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r2.speaker: الخليل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r2.claim: Khalil reads “my affair is beautiful patience”: patience is my manner and what I adopt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r2.anchor: قال الخليل المعنى فشأني صبر جميل والذي أعتقده صبر جميل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes the nominative “beautiful patience” as Jacob consoling himself: all he has is patience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء الصبر مرفوع لأنه عزى نفسه وقال ما هو إلا الصبر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r4.speaker: قطرب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r4.claim: Qutrub explains the phrase as “my patience is beautiful”; Ibn Masʿud, Ubayy, and Abu al-Mutawakkil read it in the accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r4.anchor: وقال قطرب المعنى فصبري صبر جميل وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبي وأبو المتوكل فصبرا جميلا بالنصب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r5.claim: Zajjaj says beautiful patience contains neither agitation nor complaint to people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج والصبر الجميل لا جزع فيه ولا شكوى إلى الناس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r6.claim: “God is the one whose help is sought” may refer to enduring their description of events or to enduring what they describe.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p193/r6.anchor: فيه قولان أحدهما على ما تصفون من الكذب والثاني على احتمال ما تصفون

JISHUMI:v5p3614/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3614/r1.speaker: أبو علي وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3614/r1.claim: Al-mustaʿān means God helps me, and through Him Jacob seeks help against their account of Joseph; another view makes it a plea for strength to endure grief.
JISHUMI:v5p3614/r1.anchor: وقيل: المستعان على الصبر في ذلك، عن أبي علي، وأبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v5p3614/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3614/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3614/r2.claim: Jacob's tears do not establish the truth of a claimant; the brothers' race was permissible because it was not condemned, and Jacob recognized their lie from his statement that their souls had enticed them.
JISHUMI:v5p3614/r2.anchor: تدل الآية على أن البكاء لا يدل على صدق دعوى الباكي

JISHUMI:v5p3614/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3614/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3614/r3.claim: The verse teaches patience during hardship and seeking God's help; a report says ʿĀʾishah answered the slanderers by comparing herself with Jacob and his sons, after which her vindication was revealed.
JISHUMI:v5p3614/r3.anchor: وتدل على وجوب الصبر عند الشدائد، ونزول المحن، والاستعانة بالله

AKHFASH:v1p396/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p396/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p396/r4.claim: The blood is called كذب because a lie was attached to it, like calling a night الهلال or saying their trade did not profit.
AKHFASH:v1p396/r4.anchor: وقال {بدم كذب} فجعل "الدم" "كذبا" لأنه كذب فيه كما تقول "الليلة الهلال"

FARRA:v2p38/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p38/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p38/r5.claim: دم كذب means “a false, fabricated blood”; Arabic can give verbal nouns passive-like forms such as مكذوب and مضعوف.
FARRA:v2p38/r5.anchor: معناه: مكذوب: والعرب تقول للكذب. مكذوب وللضعف : مضعوف

FARRA:v2p38/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p38/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p38/r6.claim: The brothers claimed a wolf had eaten Joseph and dipped his shirt in a lamb’s blood; Jacob noted the wolf had torn neither the skin nor the shirt.
FARRA:v2p38/r6.anchor: فقال: لقد كان هذا الذئب رفيقا بابني، مزق جلده ولم يمزق ثيابه.

FARRA:v2p38/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p38/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p38/r7.claim: Farra also permits بدم كذبا as an adverbial accusative, like جاءوا بأمر باطل or جاءوا باطلا.
FARRA:v2p38/r7.anchor: ويجوز في العربية أن تقول: جاءوا على قميصه بدم كذبا

FARRA:v2p38/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p38/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p38/r8.claim: Poetic usage supports passive-like forms derived from verbal nouns, including المجلود and معقولا.

FARRA:v2p38/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p38/r9.speaker: أبو ثروان
FARRA:v2p38/r9.claim: Abū Tharwān uses مكذوبة for a lie or fabricated claim.
FARRA:v2p38/r9.anchor: إن بني نمير ليس لحدهم مكذوبة

MAJAZ:v1p302/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p302/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p302/r8.claim: سولت لكم means your selves adorned and made the deed seem good, and you followed them in it.
MAJAZ:v1p302/r8.anchor: «سولت لكم أنفسكم» (18) أي زينت وحسنت، وتابعتكم على ذلك

NAHHAS:v2p317/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p317/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p317/r7.claim: He labels the construction figurative, supplying ذي كذب as in the idiom asking a village.
NAHHAS:v2p317/r7.anchor: مجاز أي ذي كذب مثل واسأل القرية

NAHHAS:v2p317/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p317/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p317/r8.claim: Abu Ishaq understands فصبر جميل as my affair or conviction is beautiful patience.
NAHHAS:v2p317/r8.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق أي فشأني أو الذي اعتقده صبر جميل

NAHHAS:v2p317/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p317/r9.speaker: قطرب
NAHHAS:v2p317/r9.claim: Qutrub paraphrases it as فصبري صبر جميل.
NAHHAS:v2p317/r9.anchor: قال قطرب أي فصبري صبر جميل

NAHHAS:v2p317/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p317/r10.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
NAHHAS:v2p317/r10.claim: Isa ibn Umar is reported by Sahl ibn Yusuf to read فصبرا جميلا in the accusative; al-Ashhab and two codices are also cited.
NAHHAS:v2p317/r10.anchor: قال أبو حاتم قرأ عيسى بن عمر فيما زعم سهل بن يوسف ( فصبرا جميلا )

NAHHAS:v2p317/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p317/r11.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v2p317/r11.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid prefers nominative because the meaning is the patience I have; accusative is preferred in commands.
NAHHAS:v2p317/r11.anchor: قال محمد بن يزيد فصبر جميل بالرفع أولى من النصب لأن المعنى فالذي عندي صبر جميل

NAHHAS:v2p317/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p317/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p317/r12.claim: Abu Jaafar analyzes the accusative as a verbal noun.
NAHHAS:v2p317/r12.anchor: قال أبو جعفر والنصب على المصدر

NAHHAS:v2p317/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p317/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p317/r13.claim: والله المستعان is subject and predicate; على ما تصفون is figurative, seeking help to endure their allegation.
NAHHAS:v2p317/r13.anchor: ( والله المستعان ) ابتداء وخبر ( على ما تصفون ) مجاز والمعنى والله أعلم والله المستعان على احتمال ما تصفون

TABATABAI:12:21#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:21#4/r1.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:21#4/r1.claim: In Abu Hamza's report, Jacob's sons planned to kill Yusuf, but their eldest persuaded them to cast him into a well; they later lied that a wolf ate him, and Jacob grieved yet trusted the truthful dream God had shown him.
TABATABAI:12:21#4/r1.anchor: فقال كبيرهم { لا تقتلوا يوسف } ولكن { ألقوه في غيابت الجب يلتقطه بعض السيارة إن كنتم فاعلين }

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r3.speaker: عامر الشعبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r3.claim: Joseph's shirt bore three signs: its tear, the false blood, and its placement on Jacob's face, which restored his sight.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r3.anchor: عن إسرائيل عن سماك بن حرب عن عامر الشعبي قال كان في قميص يوسف ثلاث آيات الشق والدم وإلقاؤه على وجهه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r4.claim: Beautiful patience means enduring without agitation or complaint.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r4.anchor: عن الثوري عن رجل عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ فصبر جميل ﴾ قال في غير جزع

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r5.speaker: بعض أصحاب الثوري
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r5.claim: Three marks of patience are not speaking of one's pain, calamity, or self-praise.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r5.anchor: عن الثوري عن بعض أصحابه قال يقال ثلاث من الصبر أن لا تحدث بوجعك ولا بمصيبتك ولا تزكي نفسك

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r6.speaker: حبيب بن أبي ثابت
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r6.claim: Jacob lifted his fallen brows with a cloth; after God rebuked his lament as complaint against Him, Jacob asked forgiveness for a mistake.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r6.anchor: عن الثوري عم حبيب بن أبي ثابت أن يعقوب النبي عليه السلام كان قد سقط حاجباه فكان يرفعهما بخرقة فقيل له

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r7.claim: Whoever recalls a calamity and says the words of resignation receives the same reward as when first struck by it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r7.anchor: عن إسرائيل عن رجل عن فاطمة بنت الحسين عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال من أصيب بمصيبة فذكرها فاسترجع

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r8.claim: He repeatedly told Hamna of her brother Abdullah, Hamza, and husband Mus'ab's deaths and had her say the words of resignation; her grief at her husband's death showed a spouse's special place.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r8.anchor: عن معمر عن الجحشي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لحمنة بنت جحش قولي إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p231#3/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p231#3/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p231#3/r14.claim: The form al-kadhib, with an un-dotted dāl, means murky or cloudy; another reported sense is fresh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p231#3/r14.anchor:
الكذب بالدال المهملة الكدر، وقيل:
الطري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p231#3/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p231#3/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p231#3/r15.claim: Sawwala derives from al-sawl and means to make easy or to adorn and make attractive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p231#3/r15.anchor: سول من السول، ومعناه سهل، وقيل: زين

TABRISI:72:1-10/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:72:1-10/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:72:1-10/r1.claim: In the example from Joseph, kadhib means false or lying.
TABRISI:72:1-10/r1.anchor: وجاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب [يوسف: 18] أي كاذب

THALABI:v1p75/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p75/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p75/r1.claim: The author says the book treats twenty-four fields, including readings, Arabic, exegesis, law, mystical allusions, virtues, and reports, woven through the work without separate chapters.
THALABI:v1p75/r1.anchor: وخرجت الكلام فيه على أربعة وعشرين نحوا: البسائط، والمقدمات، والعدد، والترتيلات، والقصص، والروايات، والوجوه والقراءات

THALABI:v1p75/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p75/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p75/r2.claim: The author lists the works underpinning his book so that he need not repeat transmission chains.
THALABI:v1p75/r2.anchor: هذه أسماء الكتب التي عليها مباني كتابنا هذا [أذكرها] لئلا نحتاج إلى تكرار الأسانيد

THALABI:v1p75/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p75/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v1p75/r3.claim: The author cites the Prophet’s prayer that Ibn Abbas be taught interpretation and granted understanding of religion, and says God answered it.
THALABI:v1p75/r3.anchor: [وقد] دعا [له] رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال:

BURHAN:v2p153/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p153/r2.speaker: يحيى ابن معاذ الرازي
BURHAN:v2p153/r2.claim: Yahya b. Muʿadh compares men’s mouths to shops and teeth to their trades: speech reveals their craft; he laments harsh times and few helpers.
BURHAN:v2p153/r2.anchor: يحيى ابن معاذ الرازي يقول افواه الرجال حوانيتها وأسنانها صنائعها فإذا فتح الرجل باب حانوته تبين العطار من البيطار

BURHAN:v2p153/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p153/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p153/r3.claim: Understanding the Quran’s subtle meanings requires deep learning and piety; its difficult subtleties and truths are grasped by an attentive listener.
BURHAN:v2p153/r3.anchor: كتاب الله بحره عميق وفهمه دقيق لايصل إلى فهمة الا من تبحر في العلوم وعامل الله بتقواه

BURHAN:v2p153/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p153/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p153/r4.claim: The Quran has outward recitation, inward understanding, legal limits, and an opening into promises and warnings; its allusive meanings address the discerning.
BURHAN:v2p153/r4.anchor: فالظاهر التلاوة والباطن الفهم والحد احكام الحلال والحرام والمطلع أي الإشراق من الوعد والوعيد

BURHAN:v2p153/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p153/r5.speaker: رسول الله
BURHAN:v2p153/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that the Prophet said the Quran was revealed on seven aḥruf and every verse has an outward and inward aspect.
BURHAN:v2p153/r5.anchor: وفي صحيح ابن حيان عن ابن مسعود قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انزل القرآن على سبعة احرف لكل آية منه ظهر وبطن

BURHAN:v2p153/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p153/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p153/r6.claim: Hearing from the reciter yields knowledge of rulings; hearing as though from the Prophet brings admonition and the subtleties of his address, while the Gabriel and divine perspectives disclose the unseen and lead to self-effacement.
BURHAN:v2p153/r6.anchor: فمن سمعه من التالي ففائدته فيه علم احكامه ومن سمعه كأنما يسمعه من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURHAN:v2p153/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p153/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
BURHAN:v2p153/r7.claim: Abu al-Darda says a person does not truly understand until he recognizes multiple aspects of the Quran.
BURHAN:v2p153/r7.anchor: وقد قال أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه لا يفقه الرجل حتى يجعل للقرآن وجها

BURHAN:v3p31/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p31/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p31/r2.claim: The world is not the arena of universal recompense; it contains punishment only as wisdom and benefit require, as with legal penalties.
BURHAN:v3p31/r2.anchor: إذ الدنيا ليس دار الجزاء العام وإنما فيها من الجزاء ما تحصل به الحكمة والمصلحة كما في العقوبات الشرعية

BURHAN:v3p31/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p31/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p31/r3.claim: A threatened believer whom God protects resembles Ibrahim and Muhammad: God turns apparent destruction into blessing, humiliates the enemy, and grants the believer the final outcome.
BURHAN:v3p31/r3.anchor: فمن أرادوا عداوة أحد من أتباع الأنبياء ليهلكوه فعصمه الله وجعل صورة الهلاك نعمة في حقه

BURHAN:v3p31/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p31/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p31/r4.claim: Ibrahim and Muhammad are the two best intimate friends of God, and their paths are especially marked by compassion and mercy.
BURHAN:v3p31/r4.anchor: فإن محمدا سيد الجميع وهو خليل الله كما أن إبراهيم عليه السلام خليله والخليلان هما أفضل الجميع

BURHAN:v3p31/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p31/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p31/r5.claim: The peoples’ offenses differed: arrogance among ʿAd, worldly distraction among Thamud, financial injustice and shirk in Midian, and legalized indecency among Lot’s people; the account suggests Lot’s people were not polytheists.
BURHAN:v3p31/r5.anchor: وأما عاد فذكر عنهم التجبر وعمارة الدنيا وقوم صالح ذكر عنهم الاشتغال بالدنيا عن الأنبياء

BURHAN:v3p31/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p31/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p31/r6.claim: God’s punishments display wisdom by fitting each people’s offense; Noah’s people were all drowned because no good was hoped from them.
BURHAN:v3p31/r6.anchor: وهذه الأمور تدل على حكمة الرب وعقوبته لكل قوم بما يناسبهم ولما لم يكن في قوم نوح خير يرجى غرق الجميع

ITQAN:v2p569/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p569/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p569/r1.claim: Khashya is a stronger fear than khawf: its derivation is likened to a dry tree, signifying total loss, while khawf is likened to a diseased camel, signifying deficiency rather than loss.
ITQAN:v2p569/r1.anchor: لا شك أن الخشية أعلى منه وهي أشد الخوف فإنها مأخوذة من قولهم شجرة خشية أي يابسة وهو فوات بالكلية

ITQAN:v2p569/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p569/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p569/r2.claim: Khashya arises from the feared object’s greatness even when the fearful person is strong; khawf arises from the fearful person’s weakness even when the danger is slight.
ITQAN:v2p569/r2.anchor: وفرق بينهما أيضا بأن الخشية تكون من عظم المختشى وإن كان الخاشي قويا والخوف يكون من ضعف الخائف

ITQAN:v2p569/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p569/r5.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v2p569/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib says shuḥḥ combines greed with miserliness and is more severe than bukhl.
ITQAN:v2p569/r5.anchor: ومن ذلك الشح والبخل والشح هو أشد البخل قال الراغب الشح بخل مه حرص

ITQAN:v2p569/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p569/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p569/r8.claim: Jāʾa is used for concrete entities, whereas atā is used for meanings and times; hence the brothers came with false blood, while the command of God came.
ITQAN:v2p569/r8.anchor: ومن ذلك جاء وأتى فالأول يقال في الجواهر والأعيان والثاني في المعاني والأزمان

ITQAN:v2p476#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p476#3/r3.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v2p476#3/r3.claim: Al-Zarkashī gives a rule: praised or rewarded ẓann means certainty, while blameworthy or threatened ẓann means doubt.
ITQAN:v2p476#3/r3.anchor: وقال الزركشي في البرهان الفرق بينهما في القرآن ضابطان أحدهما أنه حيث وجد الظن محمودا مثابا عليه فهو اليقين

DAMGHANI:v1p106/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r9.claim: Jamīl can describe patience without complaint.
DAMGHANI:v1p106/r9.anchor: الرابع الجميل الذي لا شكوى فيه قوله تعالى في سورة يوسف

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r1.speaker: الطاعنون على القرآن بالمجاز
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r1.claim: Those who attack Qur’anic metaphor call it falsehood because walls do not will and villages are not questioned; Ibn Qutayba calls this gross ignorance.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r1.anchor: وأما الطاعنون على القرآن (بالمجاز) فإنهم زعموا أنه كذب. لأن الجدار لا يريد، والقرية لا تسأل.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r2.claim: If attributing an act to something inanimate made speech false, ordinary Arabic claims that plants grow, mountains stand, and prices fall would also be false.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r2.anchor: ولو كان المجاز كذبا، وكل فعل ينسب إلى غير الحيوان باطلا- كان أكثر كلامنا فاسدا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r5.claim: In “false blood,” the blood is not itself lying; the brothers lied by means of it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r5.anchor: ويقول: وجاؤ على قميصه بدم كذب [يوسف: 18] وإنما كذب به

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r7.claim: The expression كان الله cannot imply that God began to exist: God was before everything, without beginning, and did not come into being after nonexistence.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p85/r7.anchor: وتقول: كان الله. وكان بمعنى حدث، والله، جل وعز: قبل كل شيء بلا غاية

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r9.claim: Jacob's nominative fa-ṣabrun implies a nominal sentence and lifelong, enduring patience; accusative fa-ṣabran would imply a temporary act of patience.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#3/r9.anchor: فجاء بالصبر مرفوعاً أي: بتقدير الجملة الاسمية لأنه وَطَّنَ نفسه على الصبر الطويل الدائم الذي لا يعرف له نهاية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p462/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p462/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p462/r1.claim: The brothers' shirt bearing false blood remains intact; “preyed on him” would imply torn clothes, so Samarrai notes the wording “ate him” instead.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p462/r1.anchor: والافتراس يفترض أن يمزق ثيابه كلها وإخوة يوسف جاءوا على قميصه بدم كذب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1103/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1103/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1103/r1.claim: The blood-stained shirt was fabricated evidence for the brothers' claim that a wolf had eaten Joseph.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1103/r1.anchor: هذه بينة مزورة وليست بيّنة صحيحة (بدم كذب)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1104/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1104/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1104/r1.claim: The false-blood shirt marks the beginning of Jacob’s grief, while Joseph’s later shirt marks its end.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1104/r1.anchor: الأمر الآخر أنه استُعمل بداية لحزن يعقوب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1104/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1104/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1104/r2.claim: Joseph’s shirt is evidence at three stages: his separation into slavery, imprisonment after the Aziz’s wife incident, and reunion with his family.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1104/r2.anchor: استعمل القميص بيّنة في ثلاث مواضع واستعمل لثلاث مراحل زمنية معاشية في حياة يوسف

SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.claim: Expressions such as حمدا، شكرا، عجبا and كرامة are accusatives governed by an omitted verb; they replace explicit forms such as أحمد الله or أشكر الله.
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.anchor: فإنما ينتصب هذا على إضمار الفعل

SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.claim: Yunus reports that Ru'bah recited a line with عجب raised; Sibawayh uses it to show that such expressions can instead form a nominal clause.
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.anchor: كان ينشد هذا البيت رفعا وهو لبعض مذحج

SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.claim: A trusted Arab's reply حمد الله وثناء عليه is raised as a nominal statement, with an implied topic such as أمري or شأني, rather than an omitted verb.

SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.claim: Sibawayh parses فصبر جميل as a raised nominal clause meaning الأمر صبر جميل; the accusative version is more common and apt when directly exhorting someone.

SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.claim: In examples such as من أنت زيد, Arabic can omit the raising topic just as it omits the verb in accusative expressions, preserving the intended nominal sense.
SIBAWAYH:منذلكقولكحمداوشكرالاكفراوعجباوأ.anchor: فتركوا إظهار الرافع كترك إظهار الناصب

NASHR:v1p320#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p320#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p320#2/r1.claim: The first degree is pure short madd in a separated syllable: remove incidental extension and leave the long-vowel letter unchanged; Abu Jaʿfar and Ibn Kathir use it throughout, though two works imply more.
NASHR:v1p320#2/r1.anchor: قصر المنفصل، وهي حذف المد العرضي، وإبقاء ذات حرف المد على ما فيها من غير زيادة

NASHR:v1p320#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p320#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p320#2/r2.claim: Many authorities assign qasr on all Qalun routes; other manuals make it one of two options, and al-Dani read it from Abu al-Fath Faris.
NASHR:v1p320#2/r2.anchor: أما قالون فقطع له بالقصر أبو بكر بن مجاهد وأبو بكر بن مهران وأبو طاهر بن سوار وأبو علي البغدادي وأبو العز

NASHR:v1p320#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p320#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p320#2/r3.claim: Most eastern and western compilers assign qasr to al-Asbahani from Warsh; one manual presents it as one of two options.
NASHR:v1p320#2/r3.anchor: وأما الأصبهاني، عن ورش فقطع له بالقصر أكثر المؤلفين من المشارقة والمغاربة، كابن مجاهد، وابن مهران

NASHR:v1p320#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p320#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p320#2/r4.claim: Many authorities assign qasr to both Abu Amr transmissions; it is one of Ibn Mujahid's options and is restricted in some works to the idgham route.
NASHR:v1p320#2/r4.anchor: وأما أبو عمرو فقطع له بالقصر من روايتيه ابن مهران

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r1.claim: Regional readers followed transmitted variants, especially those matching the codex’s consonantal outline, and exercised judgment; this yielded the seven canonical readers and others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r1.anchor: ثم إن القراء في الأمصار تتبعوا ما روي لهم من اختلافات لا سيما فيما وافق خط المصحف، فقرؤوا بذلك حسب اجتهاداتهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r2.claim: The seven readings became established by consensus and are used in prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r2.anchor: ومضت الأعصار والأمصار على قراءة السبعة وبها يصلى لأنها ثبتت بالإجماع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r3.claim: Anomalous readings are not used in prayer because the community did not agree on them; those transmitted from Companions and leading Successors are still treated as genuinely transmitted by them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r3.anchor: وأما شاذ القراءات فلا يصلى به، وذلك لأنه لم يجمع الناس عليه. أما أن المروي منه عن الصحابة رضي الله عنهم وعن علماء التابعين لا يعتقد فيه إلا أنهم رووه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r4.claim: Readings attributed to Abū al-Sammāl and similar figures are not reliable, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya records them so they will not be unknown.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r4.anchor: وأما ما يؤثر عن أبي السمال ومن قاربه فلا يوثق به وإنما أذكره في هذا الكتاب لئلا يجهل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r5.claim: The early codex lacked vowel marks and dots; Ibn ʿAṭiyya briefly summarizes disputes over this subject and relies on what he considers a clear, sound method.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p48/r5.anchor: وكان المصحف غير مشكول ولا منقوط، وقد وقع لبعض الناس خلاف في بعض ما ذكرته في هذا الباب ومنازعات اختصرت ذلك كراهة التطويل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-Muhaymin as the trustworthy Qur'an, entrusted over every earlier scripture; Ibn Kathir relates this to Qur'an 5:48.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: المهيمن الأمين القرآن، أمين على كل كتاب قبله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r2.claim: Al-Bukhari placed Qur'an virtues after tafsir because tafsir is more important; Ibn Kathir instead puts virtues first, including each surah's merit before its commentary, to encourage memorization, understanding, and practice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r2.anchor: ذكر البخاري، رحمه الله، كتاب "فضائل القرآن" بعد كتاب التفسير؛ لأن التفسير أهم ولهذا بدأ به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains al-Muhaymin as a witness over the preceding scriptures.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r4.claim: In a report through Sufyan al-Thawri and other leading authorities, Ibn Abbas glosses al-Muhaymin as entrusted over the earlier books.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r4.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق السبيعي، عن التميمي، عن ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r5.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وقتادة وابن جريج والحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r5.claim: Mujahid, al-Suddi, Qatada, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Hasan al-Basri share this entrusted or trustworthy sense of al-Muhaymin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r5.anchor: وبنحو ذلك قال مجاهد والسدي وقتادة وابن جريج والحسن البصري وغير واحد من أئمة السلف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r6.claim: The root sense of haymana is guarding and watching; al-Muhaymin as a divine name means witness, overseer, and preserver of everything.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r6.anchor: وأصل الهيمنة: الحفظ والارتقاب، يقال إذا رقب الرجل الشيء وحفظه وشهده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r7.speaker: عائشة وابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r7.claim: A report from Aisha and Ibn Abbas says the Prophet received Qur'an in Mecca for ten years and in Medina for ten; Ibn Kathir says al-Bukhari alone includes it among the two Sahihs, while al-Nasa'i also transmits it from Aisha.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p17/r7.anchor: عن أبي سلمة قال: أخبرتني عائشة وابن عباس قالا لبث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة عشر سنين ينزل عليه القرآن، وبالمدينة عشرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r1.speaker: السلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r1.claim: The early Muslims understood singing the Qur'an as improving the voice and reciting with a sorrowful, affecting tone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r1.anchor: فقد فهم من هذا أن السلف، رضي الله عنهم، إنما فهموا من التغني بالقرآن: إنما هو تحسين الصوت به، وتحزينه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r2.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r2.claim: Al-Bara' reports the Prophet's instruction to beautify the Qur'an with one's voice; Ibn Kathir calls the chain good and notes corroborating routes in al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r3.speaker: يحيى بن سعيد القطان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r3.claim: Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Hibban regarded Abd al-Rahman b. Awsaja as trustworthy, but al-Azdi reports that Yahya b. Sa'id al-Qattan did not approve of him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r3.anchor: ونقل الأزدي عن يحيى بن سعيد القطان أنه قال: سألت عنه بالمدينة، فلم أرهم يحمدونه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r4.claim: Abu Ubayd reports that Ayub told Shu'ba not to transmit the beautifying-voices hadith; Abu Ubayd supposes Ayub feared people would take it as permission for invented melodies.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r4.anchor: نهاني أيوب أن أحدث بهذا الحديث: "زينوا القرآن بأصواتكم". قال أبو عبيد: وإنما كره أيوب فيما نرى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects withholding a sound report merely because someone might misinterpret it: that would discard much Sunnah, just as people have distorted Qur'anic verses from their intended legal senses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r5.anchor: ولو ترك كل حديث بتأول مبطل لترك من السنة شيء كثير، بل قد تطرقوا إلى تأويل آيات كثيرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r6.claim: Beautifying recitation means making it melodious and sorrowful, with humility.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r6.anchor: والمراد من تحسين الصوت بالقرآن: تطريبه وتحزينه والتخشع به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r7.speaker: أبو موسى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r7.claim: Abu Musa says he would have ornamented his recitation had he known the Prophet was listening; Muslim adds the Prophet said he had been given one of David's family's flutes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r7.anchor: قلت: أما والله لو علمت أنك تستمع قراءتي لحبرتها لك تحبيرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir infers that deliberate vocal embellishment is permitted: Abu Musa had a fine voice, marked by deep fear and the Yemenites' tenderness, and the Prophet praised it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p62/r8.anchor: فدل على جواز تعاطي ذلك وتكلفه، وقد كان أبو موسى كما قال، عليه السلام، قد أعطي صوتا حسنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p68/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p68/r1.speaker: سهل بن سعد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p68/r1.claim: Sahl reports that a man unable to provide even an iron ring married a woman in return for what he knew of the Qur'an; the Prophet instructed him to give her what he had memorized.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p68/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p68/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p68/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir understands the man to have been required to teach the woman the Qur'an he knew, with that teaching serving as her dower.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p68/r2.anchor: وأمره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يعلمه تلك المرأة، ويكون ذلك صداقا لها على ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p68/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p68/r3.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p68/r3.claim: Scholars dispute whether Qur'an teaching may be a dower or earn a fee, whether this ruling was specific, and how to read the marriage formula; Ahmad says it means honoring the man or compensation for what he knew, which Ibn Kathir prefers because Muslim's version says “teach her.”
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p68/r3.anchor: كما قاله أحمد بن حنبل: نكرمك بذلك أو بعوض ما معك، وهذا أقوى، لقوله في صحيح مسلم: "فعلمها"

ITQAN:v3p166/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p166/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p166/r7.claim: With فصبر جميل and فتحرير رقبة, either an adjectival reading or an omitted subject such as أمري / الواجب can complete the syntax.
ITQAN:v3p166/r7.anchor: ويحتمل الأمرين ﴿ فصبر جميل ﴾ أي أجمل أو فأمري صبر

BUKHARI:4141/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4141/r1.speaker: عائشة
BUKHARI:4141/r1.claim: عائشة recounts the slander, witness testimonies supporting her innocence, her appeal to Jacob's father's patience (12:18), and revelation of ten verses vindicating her (24:11–20).
BUKHARI:4141/r1.anchor: قالت عائشة فقدمنا المدينة فاشتكيت حين قدمت شهرا، والناس يفيضون في قول أصحاب الإفك

BUKHARI:4690/r2.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4690/r2.speaker: عائشة
BUKHARI:4690/r2.claim: عائشة answers that she can only follow Jacob's father's beautiful patience (12:18), then reports that ten verses were revealed to vindicate her (24:11–20).
BUKHARI:4690/r2.anchor: عائشة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حين قال لها أهل الإفك ما قالوا فبرأها الله

IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r3.claim: Aisha refused to confess to a false accusation or repent for it, since she expected not to be believed if she denied it; she invoked Joseph's appeal for patience and God's help.
IBNHISHAM:v2p301#2/r3.anchor: ولكن سأقول كما قال أبو يوسف: «فصبر جميل، والله المستعان على ما تصفون»

MUSLIM:7021/r2.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:7021/r2.speaker: أبو يوسف
MUSLIM:7021/r2.claim: Aisha rejects a false confession and invokes Abu Yusuf (Jacob), saying beautiful patience and asking God's help against the accusation.
MUSLIM:7021/r2.anchor: كما قال أبو يوسف فصبر جميل والله المستعان على ما تصفون
